Rearranging gives \(\tfrac{2\gamma{\varepsilon}}{1-\gamma}\).
cards.ex: Q-learning output with \({\lVert \widehat Q-Q^\star\rVert}_\infty\le0.01\) and \(\gamma=0.9\): the greedy policy is \(0.2\)-optimal.
cards.use: Converting \(Q\)-estimation guarantees into policy guarantees (Q-learning, FQI, model-based planning).

cards.name: Policy gradient theorem
cards.lay: The gradient of a policy's value equals the expected \(Q\)-value times the gradient of the log-probability of the action, averaged over states the policy visits. Remarkably, you never need to differentiate the state distribution — so it can be estimated from rollouts without a model.
cards.st: (Sutton et al. 2000) For a differentiable policy \(\pi_\theta\): \[ \nabla_\theta V^{\pi_\theta}(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}{\mathbb{E}}_{s\sim d^{\pi_\theta}_\rho}{\mathbb{E}}_{a\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot|s)}\bigl[Q^{\pi_\theta}(s,a)\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a|s)\bigr]. \]
ver: Advantage form: \(Q^{\pi}\) may be replaced by \(A^\pi\) or \(Q^\pi-b(s)\) for any state baseline.

Trajectory (REINFORCE) form: \(\nabla V={\mathbb{E}}_\tau\bigl[\sum_t\gamma^t\nabla\log\pi_\theta(a_t|s_t)\sum_{t'\ge t}\gamma^{t'-t}r_{t'}\bigr]\) Log-derivative (score-function) trick & differentiating under the integral.

Deterministic policy gradient (Silver et al. 2014): \(
abla V=	frac{1}{1-\gamma}{\mathbb{E}}_{s\sim d^\mu} igl[
abla_	heta\mu_	heta(s)
abla_aQ^\mu(s,a)|_{a=\mu_	heta(s)} igr]\).

Softmax tabular: \(\tfrac{\partial V^{\pi_\theta}(\rho)}{\partial\theta_{s,a}}=\tfrac{1}{1-\gamma}d^{\pi_\theta}_\rho(s)\pi_\theta(a|s)A^{\pi_\theta}(s,a)\) Softmax policy gradient: smoothness & convergence.
Average-reward version with stationary distribution \(d^\pi\) and differential \(Q\).
cards.det: Proof. Differentiate the Bellman equation \(V^\pi(s)=\sum_a\pi(a|s)Q^\pi(s,a)\): \( abla V(s)=\sum_a abla\pi(a|s)Q(s,a)+\gamma\sum_a\pi(a|s)\sum_{s'}P(s'|s,a) abla V(s')\). Unroll the recursion (Neumann series Neumann series & the resolvent \((I-\gamma P)^{-1}\)): \( abla V( ho)=\sum_t\gamma^t{\mathbb{E}}_{s_t}\sum_a abla\pi(a|s_t)Q(s_t,a)\) and use \( abla\pi=\pi abla\log\pi\) Log-derivative (score-function) trick & differentiating under the integral.
cards.ex: Gaussian policy \(\pi_\theta(a|s)={\mathcal{N}}(\theta^\top\phi(s),\sigma^2)\): \(\nabla\log\pi=\tfrac{(a-\theta^\top\phi(s))\phi(s)}{\sigma^2}\), so the PG estimator is \(\tfrac{1}{\sigma^2}{\mathbb{E}}[(a-\theta^\top\phi)\phi\,\hat Q]\).
cards.use: REINFORCE, actor–critic, PPO/TRPO derivations, convergence analyses of PG methods, meta-gradients.

cards.name: Softmax policy gradient: smoothness & convergence
cards.lay: For tabular softmax policies, the value is a smooth function of the logits, gradient ascent never decreases value, and it converges to the optimum at rate \(O(1/t)\) — but with constants that can be exponentially bad in the worst case.
cards.st: (Mei, Xiao, Szepesvári, Schuurmans 2020) With \(\pi_\theta(a|s)\propto e^{\theta_{s,a}}\), \(V^{\pi_\theta}(\mu)\) is \(\tfrac{8}{(1-\gamma)^3}\)-smooth, and gradient ascent with \(\eta=\tfrac{(1-\gamma)^3}{8}\) satisfies \[ V^\star(\rho)-V^{\pi_{\theta_t}}(\rho)\le\frac{16S}{c^2(1-\gamma)^6t}\Bigl\|\frac{d^{\pi^\star}_\mu}{\mu}\Bigr\|_\infty^2\Bigl\|\frac1\mu\Bigr\|_\infty, \] where \(c=\inf_t\min_s\pi_{\theta_t}(a^\star(s)|s)>0\).
ver: Entropy-regularised softmax PG converges linearly (Mei et al. 2020; Cen et al. 2021 for NPG).
Lower bound: softmax PG can take \(\Omega(\exp(S))\) iterations on chain MDPs (Li et al. 2021), so the constant \(c\) can be exponentially small.
Escort / log-barrier regularised parameterisations change the constants (Agarwal et al. 2021).
cards.det: Ingredients: descent lemma \(L\)-smoothness & the descent lemma for monotone improvement, a non-uniform Łojasiewicz inequality Gradient domination for policy optimisation lower-bounding \({\lVert \nabla V\rVert}\) by suboptimality times \(\pi(a^\star|s)\), and a proof that \(\pi_\theta(a^\star|s)\) stays bounded away from 0.
cards.ex: Two-armed bandit with softmax PG: if the initial probability of the optimal arm is tiny, progress is very slow at first (gradient \(\propto\pi(a^\star)\)), illustrating the \(1/c^2\) dependence.
cards.use: Understanding vanilla PG, motivating natural gradients and entropy regularisation.

cards.name: Natural policy gradient & policy mirror descent convergence
cards.plain: Natural policy gradient & policy mirror descent convergence
cards.lay: Natural policy gradient preconditions by the Fisher information; for softmax policies it becomes a multiplicative-weights update on each state's action distribution. Treating each state as an online-learning problem and gluing with the PDL gives dimension-free \(O(1/T)\) convergence.
cards.st: (Agarwal et al. 2021) For tabular softmax NPG, equivalently \(\pi_{t+1}(a|s)\propto\pi_t(a|s)\exp\bigl(\tfrac{\eta}{1-\gamma}A^{\pi_t}(s,a)\bigr)\), starting from uniform \(\pi_0\): \[ V^\star(\rho)-V^{\pi_T}(\rho)\le\frac{\log|{\mathcal{A}}|}{\eta T}+\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)^2T}. \] With \(\eta\ge(1-\gamma)^2\log|{\mathcal{A}}|\) this is \(\le\frac{2}{(1-\gamma)^2T}\).
ver: Policy mirror descent with increasing step sizes converges linearly: \(V^\star-V^{\pi_k}\le\gamma^k\cdot O(\cdot)\) (Xiao 2022; Lan 2022).
Entropy-regularised NPG: linear convergence at rate \((1-\eta\tau)^t\) (Cen et al. 2021).

Inexact \(Q\) estimates: error \({\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{stat}}\) adds \(\tfrac{2{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{stat}}}{1-\gamma}\)-type terms; with function approximation, compatible function approximation Compatible function approximation and transfer error appear.

NPG update \(	heta\leftarrow	heta+\eta F(	heta)^\dagger
abla V(	heta)\) with Fisher \(F={\mathbb{E}}_{d^\pi}{\mathbb{E}}_\pi[
abla\log\pi
abla\log\pi^	op]\).
cards.det: Proof: per state, NPG is Hedge/OMD Online mirror descent (OMD) lemma with “gains” \(A^{\pi_t}(s,\cdot)\); its regret against \(\pi^\star(\cdot|s)\) is \(\le\tfrac{\log|{\mathcal{A}}|}{\eta}+\ldots\). The PDL Performance difference lemma (Kakade–Langford) weighted by \(d^{\pi^\star}_\rho\) turns the sum of per-state regrets into \(\sum_t(V^\star-V^{\pi_t})\); monotone improvement of NPG makes the last iterate as good as the average.
cards.ex: Dimension-free: unlike vanilla softmax PG, the NPG bound has no \(S\), no mismatch coefficient and no \(\min\pi(a^\star|s)\).
cards.use: NPG/TRPO/PPO theory, policy optimisation in adversarial and non-stationary MDPs (OMD per state), actor–critic with linear critics.
cards.ll: Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade & Sun — RL Theory book

cards.name: LP formulation of MDPs & its dual
cards.plain: LP formulation of MDPs & its dual
cards.lay: Finding an optimal value function is a linear program (smallest \(V\) satisfying all Bellman inequalities), and its dual is a linear program over occupancy measures (maximise expected reward subject to flow constraints). Duality ties values and occupancies together.
cards.st: Primal: \(\min_V\ (1-\gamma){\langle \rho, V\rangle}\) s.t. \(V(s)\ge r(s,a)+\gamma P(\cdot|s,a)^\top V\) for all \((s,a)\). Dual: \[ \max_{d\ge0}\ \sum_{s,a}d(s,a)r(s,a)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\sum_ad(s,a)=(1-\gamma)\rho(s)+\gamma\sum_{s',a'}P(s|s',a')d(s',a')\ \ \forall s. \] Optimal primal \(=V^\star\) (where \(\rho>0\)), optimal dual \(=d^{\pi^\star}_\rho\), and both have value \((1-\gamma)V^\star(\rho)\).
ver: Lagrangian (saddle-point) form: \(\min_V\max_{d\ge0}\ (1-\gamma){\langle \rho, V\rangle}+\sum_{s,a}d(s,a)\bigl[r+\gamma PV-V\bigr](s,a)\) — basis of primal–dual RL algorithms and DICE methods.
Constrained MDPs: add \(\sum d\,g\ge b\) to the dual LP; zero duality gap Lagrangian duality & Slater's condition.
Average reward LP: maximise \({\langle d, r\rangle}\) over stationary occupancies.
cards.det: Complementary slackness Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions: \(d^\star(s,a)>0\) only where \(V^\star(s)=r(s,a)+\gamma P(\cdot|s,a)^\top V^\star\), i.e. on optimal actions. The LP view gives strongly polynomial algorithms (Ye 2011) and is the foundation of saddle-point methods for sample-efficient planning.
cards.ex: Adversarial MDPs with known dynamics (O-REPS): run online mirror descent with negative-entropy regulariser directly over the occupancy polytope; regret \({\widetilde{O}}(H\sqrt{T\log(SA)})\).
cards.use: CMDPs, adversarial MDPs, DICE off-policy estimation, primal–dual sample complexity, inverse RL.

cards.name: Concentrability coefficients & error propagation
cards.lay: Errors made under one distribution (the data's) must be transferred to the distributions the evaluated or learned policies actually visit. Concentrability coefficients bound this density ratio; offline and approximate RL bounds scale with them.
cards.st: Single-policy concentrability: \(C^{\pi}=\Bigl\|\frac{d^{\pi}_\rho}{\mu}\Bigr\|_\infty\). (Munos 2007; Munos & Szepesvári 2008) For approximate VI with \({\lVert V_{k+1}-T^\star V_k\rVert}_{2,\mu}\le{\varepsilon}\): \[ \limsup_{k\to\infty}{\lVert V^\star-V^{\pi_k}\rVert}_{1,\rho}\le\frac{2\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2}\sqrt{C_{\rho,\mu}}\;{\varepsilon}, \] where \(C_{\rho,\mu}\) is a (discounted, all-policy) concentrability coefficient.
ver: Pessimistic offline RL needs only single-policy concentrability \(C^{\pi^\star}\) (Rashidinejad et al. 2021; Xie et al. 2021).
Linear-feature analogue: relative condition number \(\sup_v\tfrac{v^\top\Sigma_{\pi}v}{v^\top\Sigma_\mu v}\) Rayleigh quotient & Courant–Fischer min–max.
Distribution mismatch in policy gradient: \({\lVert d^{\pi^\star}_\rho/\mu\rVert}_\infty\) Gradient domination for policy optimisation.

Change of measure for \(L^1\): \({\mathbb{E}}_{d^\pi}|f|\le C^\pi{\mathbb{E}}_\mu|f|\); for \(L^2\): \({\mathbb{E}}_{d^\pi}|f|\le\sqrt{C^\pi{\mathbb{E}}_\mu f^2}\) (Cauchy–Schwarz Cauchy–Schwarz inequality).
cards.det: Mechanism: the error \(V^\star-V^{\pi_K}\) is a sum over past iterations of products of transition matrices applied to per-iteration errors \({\varepsilon}_k\). Bounding \(\rho^\top(P^{\pi_1}\cdots P^{\pi_m})|{\varepsilon}_k|\) in terms of \({\lVert {\varepsilon}_k\rVert}_\mu\) requires the density ratio of the pushed-forward distribution w.r.t. \(\mu\) — that is the concentrability coefficient.
cards.ex: If the data distribution \(\mu\) is uniform over \(S\) states, \(C^\pi\le S\) for every \(\pi\); if \(\mu\) never visits a state \(\pi^\star\) reaches, \(C^{\pi^\star}=\infty\) and no offline guarantee is possible.
cards.use: Offline RL, FQI/FVI bounds, pessimism, policy gradient exploration conditions, off-policy evaluation.

cards.name: Projected Bellman equation & TD fixed point (Tsitsiklis–Van Roy)
cards.plain: Projected Bellman equation & TD fixed point (Tsitsiklis–Van Roy)
cards.lay: With linear function approximation, TD learning does not find the best approximation of \(V^\pi\); it finds the fixed point of the projected Bellman operator. On-policy, that operator is a contraction and the fixed point is within a \(1/\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}\) factor of the best approximation.
cards.st: Let \(\mu\) be the stationary distribution of \(P^\pi\), \(D={\operatorname{diag}}(\mu)\), \(\Pi\) the \({\lVert \cdot\rVert}_D\)-projection onto \(\{\Phi\theta\}\). Then \(\Pi T^\pi\) is a \(\gamma\)-contraction in \({\lVert \cdot\rVert}_D\), TD(0) converges to its fixed point \(\Phi\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}\), and \[ {\lVert \Phi\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}-V^\pi\rVert}_D\le\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}}\min_\theta{\lVert \Phi\theta-V^\pi\rVert}_D. \]
ver: Key lemma: \({\lVert P^\pi V\rVert}_D\le{\lVert V\rVert}_D\) when \(D\) is stationary (Jensen Jensen's inequality).
TD(\(\lambda\)): factor \(\tfrac{1-\lambda\gamma}{1-\gamma}\) (Tsitsiklis & Van Roy 1997); as \(\lambda\to1\) it recovers the best approximation.
Off-policy: \(\Pi_DT^\pi\) need not be a contraction — Baird's counterexample; motivates GTD/TDC and emphatic TD.

Finite-time: \({\mathbb{E}}{\lVert \theta_T-\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}\rVert}^2={\widetilde{O}}\bigl(\tfrac{t_{\mathrm{mix}}}{(1-\gamma)^2\omega^2T}\bigr)\) with \(\omega=\lambda_{\min}(\Phi^\top D\Phi)\) (Bhandari, Russo, Singal 2018).
cards.det: Contraction: \({\lVert \Pi T^\pi V-\Pi T^\pi U\rVert}_D\le{\lVert T^\pi V-T^\pi U\rVert}_D=\gamma{\lVert P^\pi(V-U)\rVert}_D\le\gamma{\lVert V-U\rVert}_D\), using non-expansiveness of the projection Projection theorem & non-expansiveness of projections and stationarity. The approximation bound follows from Pythagoras: \({\lVert V^\pi-\Phi\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}\rVert}^2={\lVert V^\pi-\Pi V^\pi\rVert}^2+{\lVert \Pi V^\pi-\Pi T^\pi\Phi\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}\rVert}^2\le{\lVert V^\pi-\Pi V^\pi\rVert}^2+\gamma^2{\lVert V^\pi-\Phi\theta_{\mathrm{TD}}\rVert}^2\).
cards.ex: With \(\gamma=0.99\) the factor \(1/\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}\approx7.1\): TD's fixed point can be up to \(7\times\) worse than the best linear fit in \({\lVert \cdot\rVert}_D\).
cards.use: Linear TD/LSTD analysis, actor–critic critics, understanding the deadly triad, finite-sample TD bounds.

cards.name: Conservative policy iteration & TRPO improvement bound
cards.plain: Conservative policy iteration & TRPO improvement bound
cards.lay: If the new policy is close to the old one (in TV or KL), you can predict its performance using the old policy's state distribution, with an error quadratic in the distance. Optimising this surrogate guarantees monotone improvement.
cards.st: (Kakade & Langford 2002; Schulman et al. 2015) Let \(L_\pi(\pi')=V^\pi(\rho)+\tfrac{1}{1-\gamma}{\mathbb{E}}_{s\sim d^\pi_\rho}{\mathbb{E}}_{a\sim\pi'}A^\pi(s,a)\), \(\epsilon=\max_{s,a}|A^\pi(s,a)|\), \(\alpha=\max_s{\mathrm{TV}}(\pi(\cdot|s),\pi'(\cdot|s))\). Then \[ V^{\pi'}(\rho)\ge L_\pi(\pi')-\frac{4\gamma\epsilon\,\alpha^2}{(1-\gamma)^2}. \]
ver: KL version (via Pinsker Pinsker's inequality): \(\alpha^2\le\tfrac12\max_s{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi(\cdot|s)\|\pi'(\cdot|s))\).

CPI with mixture \(\pi'=(1-\alpha)\pi+\alpha\pi_{\mathrm{greedy}}\): improvement \(\ge\tfrac{\alpha}{1-\gamma}\mathbb A-\tfrac{2\alpha^2\gamma\epsilon}{(1-\gamma)^2}\) where \(\mathbb A\) is the average advantage.
cards.det: Proof: PDL Performance difference lemma (Kakade–Langford) gives the exact gap with \(d^{\pi'}\); the surrogate uses \(d^\pi\). The two state distributions differ in TV by at most \(\tfrac{\gamma\alpha}{1-\gamma}\)-ish (coupling the policies Coupling inequality), and the expected advantage of \(\pi'\) under \(\pi\) is itself \(O(\alpha\epsilon)\) since \({\mathbb{E}}_{a\sim\pi}A^\pi=0\); multiplying gives the \(\alpha^2\) term.
cards.ex: Monotone improvement: maximise \(L_\pi(\pi')-C\max_s{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi\|\pi')\) with \(C=\tfrac{2\gamma\epsilon}{(1-\gamma)^2}\); the result is never worse than \(\pi\) (TRPO's theoretical motivation).
cards.use: Trust-region methods, PPO clipping motivation, safe policy improvement, CPI analysis.

cards.name: Compatible function approximation
cards.lay: If the critic's features are exactly the policy's score function \(\nabla\log\pi_\theta\), then plugging the best linear critic into the policy gradient gives the exact gradient. Also shows the NPG direction is the least-squares fit of advantages on score features.
cards.st: (Sutton et al. 2000; Kakade 2001) Let \(w^\star={\operatorname*{arg\,min}}_w{\mathbb{E}}_{s\sim d^\pi,a\sim\pi} igl(w^ op abla_ heta\log\pi_ heta(a|s)-A^\pi(s,a) igr)^2\). Then \[ abla_ heta V^{\pi_ heta}= rac{1}{1-\gamma}F( heta)w^\star,\qquad ext{so}\qquad F( heta)^\dagger abla_ heta V^{\pi_ heta}= rac{w^\star}{1-\gamma}, \] where \(F( heta)={\mathbb{E}}_{d^\pi,\pi}[ abla\log\pi abla\log\pi^ op]\). The natural gradient is the advantage regression coefficient.
ver: Log-linear policies \(\pi\propto e^{\theta^\top\phi(s,a)}\): score features are centred features \(\phi-{\mathbb{E}}_\pi\phi\); NPG \(=\) regressing \(Q\) onto \(\phi\) (Q-NPG).

With approximation error \({\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{approx}}\), NPG converges up to \(\tfrac{\sqrt{|{\mathcal{A}}|\kappa\,{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{approx}}}}{(1-\gamma)^{3/2}}\)-type terms (Agarwal et al. 2021).
cards.det: Proof: the first-order optimality condition of the regression is \({\mathbb{E}}[ abla\log\pi( abla\log\pi^ op w^\star-A^\pi)]=0\), i.e. \(Fw^\star={\mathbb{E}}[ abla\log\pi\,A^\pi]=(1-\gamma) abla V\) by the PG theorem Policy gradient theorem.
cards.ex: Tabular softmax: score features are \(e_{s,a}-\pi(\cdot|s)\); the regression recovers \(w^\star_{s,a}=A^\pi(s,a)\), so NPG is \(\theta\leftarrow\theta+\tfrac{\eta}{1-\gamma}A^\pi\) — the multiplicative weights update of Natural policy gradient & policy mirror descent convergence.
cards.use: Natural actor–critic, NPG with function approximation, understanding critic bias in actor–critic.
cards.ll: Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade & Sun — RL Theory book

cards.name: Regret decomposition (bandits)
cards.lay: Total regret equals, for each suboptimal arm, how much worse it is times how often you pull it. So bounding regret reduces to bounding the number of pulls of each bad arm.
cards.st: For a stochastic \(K\)-armed bandit with gaps \(\Delta_a=\mu^\star-\mu_a\) and pull counts \(N_a(T)\): \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}_T=T\mu^\star-{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{t=1}^TX_t=\sum_{a}\Delta_a\,{\mathbb{E}}[N_a(T)]. \]
ver: Gap-dependent to gap-independent: split arms at threshold \(\Delta\): \({\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le T\Delta+\sum_{a:\Delta_a>\Delta}\Delta_a{\mathbb{E}} N_a(T)\); with \({\mathbb{E}} N_a\lesssim\tfrac{\log T}{\Delta_a^2}\) this gives \(O(\sqrt{KT\log T})\).

MDP analogue: \({\mathrm{Reg}}_K=\sum_{k}\bigl(V^\star_1(s_1^k)-V^{\pi_k}_1(s_1^k)\bigr)=\sum_k{\mathbb{E}}_{\pi_k}\sum_h\mathrm{gap}_h(s_h,a_h)\) via the PDL Performance difference lemma (Kakade–Langford) — gap-dependent RL bounds.
Pseudo-regret vs. realised regret: they differ by a martingale Azuma–Hoeffding inequality (martingales).
cards.det: Proof: \({\mathbb{E}}\sum_tX_t=\sum_a\mu_a{\mathbb{E}} N_a(T)\) by the tower property Tower property & law of total expectation (Wald-like Wald's identity), and \(\sum_a{\mathbb{E}} N_a(T)=T\).
cards.ex: UCB1 has \({\mathbb{E}} N_a(T)\le\tfrac{8\log T}{\Delta_a^2}+1+\tfrac{\pi^2}{3}\), so \({\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le\sum_{a:\Delta_a>0}\bigl(\tfrac{8\log T}{\Delta_a}+(1+\tfrac{\pi^2}{3})\Delta_a\bigr)\).
cards.use: All stochastic bandit regret analyses, gap-dependent RL regret.

cards.name: Optimism principle (regret \(\le\) sum of confidence widths)
cards.plain: Optimism principle (regret ≤ sum of confidence widths)
cards.lay: If your index is an upper bound on the true value of every action (optimism), then the regret of picking the largest index is at most the width of the confidence interval of the action you picked. Exploration happens automatically: uncertain actions look good until tried.
cards.st: Suppose on a good event, for all \(t\) and \(a\): \(\mu_a\le U_t(a)\) and \(U_t(a)-\mu_a\le2w_t(a)\). If \(A_t={\operatorname*{arg\,max}}_aU_t(a)\), then \[ \mu^\star-\mu_{A_t}\le U_t(A_t)-\mu_{A_t}\le2w_t(A_t),\qquad{\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le2\sum_{t=1}^Tw_t(A_t)+T\Pr(\text{bad event}). \]
ver: Linear bandits: \(w_t(x)=\beta_t{\lVert x\rVert}_{V_{t-1}^{-1}}\), summed with the elliptical potential lemma Elliptical potential lemma \(\Rightarrow{\widetilde{O}}(d\sqrt T)\).

Tabular RL: optimistic \(Q\)-values plus value-difference decomposition Value-difference (Bellman-error telescoping) decomposition \(\Rightarrow\) regret \(\le\sum_{k,h}\)(bonus) \(+\) martingale terms; bonuses summed with the pigeonhole lemma Pigeonhole / count-summation lemma (tabular RL).
Posterior sampling: optimism holds in expectation (Bayesian regret) rather than deterministically.
Pessimism (offline RL) is the mirror image: lower confidence bounds; suboptimality \(\le2{\mathbb{E}}_{\pi^\star}\sum(\text{widths})\).
cards.det: The proof is one line, and all the work is in (i) constructing valid confidence sets (concentration + union bounds) and (ii) showing widths at played actions sum to \(o(T)\) (potential or pigeonhole arguments).
cards.ex: \(K\)-armed UCB with Hoeffding widths \(w_t(a)=\sqrt{\tfrac{2\log(1/\delta)}{N_a}}\): \(\sum_tw_t(A_t)=\sum_a\sum_{n=1}^{N_a(T)}\sqrt{\tfrac{2\log(1/\delta)}{n}}\le\sum_a2\sqrt{2N_a\log(1/\delta)}\le2\sqrt{2KT\log(1/\delta)}\).
cards.use: UCB, OFUL, UCRL2, UCBVI, LSVI-UCB, GOLF; offline pessimism (mirror argument).

cards.name: Pigeonhole / count-summation lemma (tabular RL)
cards.lay: Summing \(1/\sqrt{\text{visit count}}\) over all visits is at most about \(\sqrt{(\#\text{cells})\times(\#\text{visits})}\). This converts per-step bonuses into \(\sqrt{SAT}\)-type regret.
cards.st: Let \((x_t)_{t\le T}\) take values in a finite set of size \(N\) and \(n_t(x)=\sum_{s<t}{\mathbf{1}}\{x_s=x\}\). Then \[ \sum_{t=1}^T\frac{1}{\sqrt{\max(1,n_t(x_t))}}\le N+2\sqrt{NT},\qquad\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{1}{\max(1,n_t(x_t))}\le N(2+\log T). \]
ver: Tabular RL: with \(x_t=(s_h^k,a_h^k,h)\), \(N=SAH\), \(T=KH\): \(\sum_{k,h}\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\le SAH+2\sqrt{SAH\cdot KH}\).
Weighted counts / doubling epochs (UCRL2): \(\sum_k\tfrac{\nu_k(s,a)}{\sqrt{\max(1,N_k(s,a))}}\le(\sqrt2+1)\sqrt{N(s,a)}\).
Generalisations: elliptical potential (linear) Elliptical potential lemma, eluder dimension (general classes) Eluder dimension.
cards.det: Proof: group the sum by value of \(x\): \(\sum_x\sum_{n=0}^{N_T(x)-1}\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\max(1,n)}}\le\sum_x\bigl(1+2\sqrt{N_T(x)}\bigr)\) by Sums of \(1/\sqrt{t}\), harmonic sums & integral comparison, then Cauchy–Schwarz Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: \(\sum_x\sqrt{N_T(x)}\le\sqrt{N\sum_xN_T(x)}=\sqrt{NT}\).
cards.ex: Q-learning with UCB-Hoeffding bonuses \(b_n=c\sqrt{H^3\iota/n}\): with \(N=SAH\) cells and \(KH\) visits, \(\sum_{k,h}b_{n_h^k}\le c\sqrt{H^3\iota}\bigl(SAH+2\sqrt{SAH\cdot KH}\bigr)={\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{H^4SAT})\) for \(T=KH\).
cards.use: Summing exploration bonuses in all tabular RL regret/PAC analyses.
cards.ll: Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade & Sun — RL Theory book

cards.name: Elliptical potential lemma
cards.lay: In linear bandits, the uncertainty of the chosen action (measured in the inverse design matrix) can only be large a limited number of times: the sum of squared uncertainties is at most \(O(d\log T)\). Each time you learn something, the “volume” of remaining uncertainty shrinks.
cards.st: Let \(V_0=\lambda I\), \(V_t=V_{t-1}+x_tx_t^\top\) with \({\lVert x_t\rVert}_2\le L\). Then \[ \sum_{t=1}^T\min\bigl(1,{\lVert x_t\rVert}^2_{V_{t-1}^{-1}}\bigr)\le2\log\frac{\det V_T}{\det V_0}\le2d\log\Bigl(1+\frac{TL^2}{d\lambda}\Bigr). \] Consequently \(\sum_{t=1}^T\min(1,{\lVert x_t\rVert}_{V_{t-1}^{-1}})\le\sqrt{2dT\log(1+TL^2/(d\lambda))}\).
ver: If \(\lambda\ge\max(1,L^2)\) the \(\min(1,\cdot)\) can be dropped.
Batched / rarely-switching versions: number of times \(\det V_t\) doubles is \(O(d\log T)\) Loewner order facts.
Kernelised: replace \(d\log T\) by information gain \(\gamma_T\) Entropy, mutual information & their chain rules; general classes: eluder dimension Eluder dimension.
Weighted (for non-stationary / heteroscedastic noise): \(V_t=\lambda I+\sum w_sx_sx_s^\top\), same bound with weighted features.
cards.det: Proof: \(\det V_t=\det V_{t-1}(1+{\lVert x_t\rVert}^2_{V_{t-1}^{-1}})\) (matrix determinant lemma Matrix determinant lemma); telescoping gives \(\sum_t\log(1+{\lVert x_t\rVert}^2_{V_{t-1}^{-1}})=\log\tfrac{\det V_T}{\det V_0}\). Use \(\min(1,u)\le2\log(1+u)\) Logarithm bounds, and AM–GM on eigenvalues for \(\det V_T\le(\lambda+TL^2/d)^d\) Spectral theorem for symmetric matrices. The second claim is Cauchy–Schwarz Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
cards.ex: OFUL regret: \({\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le2\beta_T\sum_t\min(1,{\lVert x_t\rVert}_{V_{t-1}^{-1}})\le2\beta_T\sqrt{2dT\log(1+T/(d\lambda))}={\widetilde{O}}(d\sqrt T)\) with \(\beta_T={\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt d)\) from Self-normalised bound for vector martingales (Abbasi-Yadkori et al.).
cards.use: Linear/generalised linear/kernel bandits, linear MDPs (LSVI-UCB), low-switching algorithms, non-stationary linear bandits.

cards.name: Exponential weights (Hedge) regret bound
cards.lay: Keep a weight for each expert, multiply it by \(e^{-\eta\cdot\text{loss}}\) after each round, and play proportionally to the weights. Against any sequence of bounded losses, you lose at most \(\sqrt{(T/2)\log N}\) compared to the best expert in hindsight.
cards.st: With losses \(\ell_t\in[0,1]^N\) and \(p_t(i)\propto\exp(-\eta\sum_{s<t}\ell_s(i))\): \[ \sum_{t=1}^T{\langle p_t, \ell_t\rangle}-\min_i\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(i)\le\frac{\log N}{\eta}+\frac{\eta T}{8}, \] so \(\eta=\sqrt{8\log N/T}\) gives regret \(\le\sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\log N}\).
ver: Second-order (local norm) bound: regret \(\le\tfrac{\log N}{\eta}+\eta\sum_t\sum_ip_t(i)\ell_t(i)^2\) for \(\eta\ell\ge-1\) — needed for EXP3 EXP3 & importance-weighted loss estimators.
Anytime: \(\eta_t=\sqrt{\log N/t}\) gives \(O(\sqrt{T\log N})\) without knowing \(T\).

Infinite/continuous experts with prior \(\pi\): regret \(\le\tfrac{{\mathrm{KL}}(\rho\|\pi)}{\eta}+\tfrac{\eta T}{8}\) against any \(\rho\) (PAC-Bayes flavour) Donsker–Varadhan & Gibbs variational principle.
It is OMD/FTRL with negative entropy Online mirror descent (OMD) lemma, Follow-the-regularised-leader (FTRL) regret bound.
cards.det: Potential proof: \(\Phi_t=\tfrac1\eta\log\sum_ie^{-\eta L_t(i)}\). Hoeffding's lemma Hoeffding's lemma gives \(\Phi_{t+1}-\Phi_t\le-{\langle p_t, \ell_t\rangle}+\tfrac{\eta}{8}\); telescope Telescoping sums from \(\Phi_0=\tfrac{\log N}{\eta}\), and use \(\Phi_T\ge-\min_iL_T(i)\) (log-sum-exp sandwich Log-sum-exp (soft-max) sandwich). Rearranging gives the bound.
cards.ex: Per-state Hedge on \(Q\)-values is NPG/policy mirror descent Natural policy gradient & policy mirror descent convergence; in adversarial MDPs with full information, running Hedge in each state with \(Q^{\pi_t}\) losses yields \({\widetilde{O}}(\tfrac{\sqrt{T\log|{\mathcal{A}}|}}{(1-\gamma)^2})\)-type regret.
cards.use: Experts, NPG/PMD, adversarial MDPs, boosting, game solving (no-regret dynamics), EXP3/EXP4.

cards.name: Follow-the-regularised-leader (FTRL) regret bound
cards.lay: Play the minimiser of past losses plus a regulariser. The regret is at most the regulariser's range divided by \(\eta\) plus a stability term. FTRL with the right regulariser recovers Hedge, OGD and many bandit algorithms.
cards.st: For linear losses \({\langle g_t, x\rangle}\) and \(x_t={\operatorname*{arg\,min}}_{x\in C}\{\eta\sum_{s<t}{\langle g_s, x\rangle}+R(x)\}\) with \(R\) \(1\)-strongly convex w.r.t. \({\lVert \cdot\rVert}\): \[ \sum_t{\langle g_t, x_t-u\rangle}\le\frac{R(u)-\min_CR}{\eta}+\eta\sum_t{\lVert g_t\rVert}_*^2\quad\forall u\in C. \]
ver: Be-the-leader lemma: \(\sum_t{\langle g_t, x_{t+1}-u\rangle}\le\tfrac{R(u)-R(x_1)}{\eta}\) (playing one step ahead has no regret).
Optimistic FTRL with hints \(m_t\): replace \({\lVert g_t\rVert}_*^2\) by \({\lVert g_t-m_t\rVert}_*^2\) — adaptivity to slowly changing losses (non-stationarity) and faster rates in games.
Tsallis-entropy FTRL achieves best-of-both-worlds bandit guarantees.
cards.det: With linear losses and unconstrained domain, FTRL and lazy OMD coincide; both play \(\nabla R^*(-\eta\sum g_s)\) Convex conjugate & Fenchel–Young.
cards.ex: Negative entropy on the simplex: \(R(u)-\min R\le\log N\), \({\lVert g\rVert}_*={\lVert g\rVert}_\infty\le1\), giving Hedge's \(O(\sqrt{T\log N})\) (constant \(2\) worse than the tight Hedge analysis).
cards.use: Adversarial bandits and MDPs (occupancy-measure FTRL), best-of-both-worlds algorithms, optimistic learning in games and non-stationary settings.

cards.name: Online gradient descent regret (Zinkevich)
cards.lay: Even against adversarially chosen convex losses, simply taking a projected gradient step each round guarantees regret \(O(DG\sqrt T)\) against the best fixed point in hindsight.
cards.st: For convex \(f_t\) on \(C\) with \(\mathrm{diam}(C)\le D\), \({\lVert \nabla f_t\rVert}\le G\), and \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(x_t-\eta_t\nabla f_t(x_t))\) with \(\eta_t=\tfrac{D}{G\sqrt t}\): \[ \sum_{t=1}^Tf_t(x_t)-\min_{u\in C}\sum_{t=1}^Tf_t(u)\le\frac32DG\sqrt T. \]
ver: \(\mu\)-strongly convex losses with \(\eta_t=\tfrac{1}{\mu t}\): regret \(\le\tfrac{G^2}{2\mu}(1+\log T)\).

Dynamic regret against a moving comparator \(u_1,\dots,u_T\) with path length \(P_T=\sum{\lVert u_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}\): \(O(\sqrt{T(1+P_T)})\) with tuned step size Dynamic regret of online gradient descent.
Exp-concave losses: Online Newton Step gives \(O(d\log T)\).
cards.det: Proof: \({\lVert x_{t+1}-u\rVert}^2\le{\lVert x_t-u\rVert}^2-2\eta_t{\langle \nabla f_t(x_t), x_t-u\rangle}+\eta_t^2G^2\) (projection is non-expansive Projection theorem & non-expansiveness of projections); convexity \(f_t(x_t)-f_t(u)\le{\langle \nabla f_t(x_t), x_t-u\rangle}\); telescope with varying \(\eta_t\) and sum \(\eta_t\) Sums of \(1/\sqrt{t}\), harmonic sums & integral comparison.
cards.ex: Online learning of a constrained MDP's Lagrange multiplier: OGD on \(\lambda\in[0,\Lambda]\) with gradients \(b-\widehat V_g\) yields dual regret \(O(\Lambda\tfrac{1}{1-\gamma}\sqrt T)\).
cards.use: Dual updates in CMDPs, online learning reductions, dynamic regret in non-stationary settings, SGD analysis Stochastic gradient descent convergence.

cards.name: Online-to-batch conversion
cards.lay: An online learner with small regret, run on i.i.d. data, yields a statistical learner: the average of its iterates has excess risk at most regret\(/T\) (plus a martingale concentration term).
cards.st: If an online algorithm achieves regret \({\mathrm{Reg}}_T\) on convex losses \(\ell(\cdot,z_t)\) with \(z_t\) i.i.d., then \(\bar x_T=\tfrac1T\sum_tx_t\) satisfies \[ {\mathbb{E}}\bigl[L(\bar x_T)\bigr]-\min_xL(x)\le\frac{{\mathbb{E}}{\mathrm{Reg}}_T}{T},\qquad L(x)={\mathbb{E}}_z\ell(x,z). \] With losses in \([0,1]\), w.p. \(\ge1-\delta\): \(L(\bar x_T)-L(u)\le\frac{{\mathrm{Reg}}_T}{T}+\sqrt{\frac{2\log(1/\delta)}{T}}\).
ver: Non-convex losses: pick a uniformly random iterate instead of the average.

In RL: regret-to-PAC — an algorithm with \({\mathrm{Reg}}_K\) over \(K\) episodes yields (by outputting a uniformly random past policy) an \(\tfrac{{\mathrm{Reg}}_K}{K}\)-optimal policy in expectation.
cards.det: Proof: \({\mathbb{E}}[\ell(x_t,z_t)\mid{\mathcal{F}}_{t-1}]=L(x_t)\) because \(x_t\) is independent of \(z_t\); hence \(\sum_t(L(x_t)-\ell(x_t,z_t))\) is a martingale Azuma–Hoeffding inequality (martingales). Jensen Jensen's inequality handles the average.
cards.ex: OGD on i.i.d. convex losses gives SGD's \(O(DG/\sqrt T)\) rate Stochastic gradient descent convergence.
cards.use: SGD rates, regret-to-PAC conversions in RL, converting adversarial algorithms to stochastic guarantees.

cards.name: Divergence decomposition for bandits
cards.lay: The KL divergence between the data distributions an algorithm sees in two bandit instances equals the sum over arms of (expected pulls in the first instance) \(\times\) (KL between that arm's reward distributions). Lower bounds start here.
cards.st: (Lattimore & Szepesvári, Lemma 15.1) For bandit instances \( u, u'\) and any policy, with \(\mathbb P_ u\) the law of the \(T\)-round history: \[ {\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbb P_ u\|\mathbb P_{ u'})=\sum_{a=1}^K{\mathbb{E}}_ u[N_a(T)]\,{\mathrm{KL}}( u_a\| u'_a). \]
ver: MDP version: \({\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbb P_M\|\mathbb P_{M'})=\sum_{s,a}{\mathbb{E}}_M[N(s,a)]{\mathrm{KL}}(P_M(\cdot|s,a)\|P_{M'}(\cdot|s,a))\) (+ reward terms) Chain rule for KL & trajectory divergence decomposition.

Combined with data processing Data-processing inequality: \(\sum_a{\mathbb{E}}_ u[N_a]{\mathrm{KL}}( u_a\| u'_a)\ge\mathrm{kl}({\mathbb{E}}_ u[Z],{\mathbb{E}}_{ u'}[Z])\) for any \([0,1]\)-valued statistic \(Z\) (Garivier et al. 2019).
cards.det: Chain rule for KL Chain rule for KL & trajectory divergence decomposition over rounds; the policy's action probabilities are identical functions of the history in both instances, so their contribution cancels.
cards.ex: Instances differing only in arm \(i\) (Gaussian, gap \(2\Delta\)): \({\mathrm{KL}}={\mathbb{E}}_\nu[N_i(T)]\cdot2\Delta^2\).
cards.use: Lai–Robbins and minimax lower bounds for bandits and MDPs, best-arm identification lower bounds, non-stationary lower bounds.

cards.name: Lai–Robbins asymptotic lower bound
cards.lay: Any algorithm that is good on every instance must pull each suboptimal arm at least \(\log T/{\mathrm{KL}}\) times, where \({\mathrm{KL}}\) measures how hard that arm is to distinguish from an arm that would be optimal. Gives the \(\log T\) regret lower bound with exact constants.
cards.st: For any consistent policy (\({\mathrm{Reg}}_T=o(T^\alpha)\) for all \(\alpha>0\) on all instances of the class) and every suboptimal arm \(a\): \[ \liminf_{T o\infty} rac{{\mathbb{E}}[N_a(T)]}{\log T}\ge rac{1}{\inf\{{\mathrm{KL}}( u_a\| u'_a):\mu( u'_a)>\mu^\star\}}. \] For Bernoulli arms: \(\liminf frac{{\mathrm{Reg}}_T}{\log T}\ge\sum_{a:\Delta_a>0} frac{\Delta_a}{\mathrm{kl}(\mu_a,\mu^\star)}\).
ver: Graves–Lai / Burnetas–Katehakis: instance-dependent lower bounds for structured bandits and MDPs as optimisation problems over exploration rates.
Gaussian arms: \(\liminf\tfrac{{\mathrm{Reg}}_T}{\log T}\ge\sum_a\tfrac{2\sigma^2}{\Delta_a}\).
cards.det: Modern proof: perturb arm \(a\) to \( u'_a\) with \(\mu( u'_a)>\mu^\star\); by the divergence decomposition and data processing Data-processing inequality, \({\mathbb{E}}_ u[N_a]{\mathrm{KL}}( u_a\| u'_a)\ge\mathrm{kl}({\mathbb{E}}_ u[N_a/T] ext{-type statistic})\approx\log T\) because a consistent algorithm must behave very differently in the two instances.
cards.ex: Bernoulli arms \(0.5\) vs. \(0.6\): \(\mathrm{kl}(0.5,0.6)\approx0.0204\), so the suboptimal arm needs \(\approx49\log T\) pulls and regret \(\ge4.9\log T\) asymptotically.
cards.use: Asymptotic optimality (KL-UCB, Thompson sampling), instance-dependent RL lower bounds.

cards.name: Minimax \(\Omega(\sqrt{KT})\) lower bound
cards.lay: No algorithm can guarantee regret smaller than about \(\sqrt{KT}\) on every \(K\)-armed bandit. The proof: hide a slightly better arm among \(K\); an algorithm that doesn't pull each arm about \(T/K\) times can't find it.
cards.st: For every policy and \(T\ge K-1\) there is a \(K\)-armed Gaussian (or Bernoulli) bandit with \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}_T\ge\frac{1}{27}\sqrt{(K-1)T}. \]
ver: Linear bandits on the hypercube: \(\Omega(d\sqrt T)\).
Episodic tabular MDPs: \(\Omega(\sqrt{H^2SAT})\)-type (with \(T=KH\) steps, horizon normalisations vary).
Non-stationary bandits with variation budget \(V_T\): \(\Omega((KV_T)^{1/3}T^{2/3})\) Lower bounds for non-stationary bandits & MDPs.
cards.det: Construction: instance \( u\) with means \((\Delta,0,\dots,0)\); let \(i={\operatorname*{arg\,min}}_{j>1}{\mathbb{E}}_ u N_j(T)\), so \({\mathbb{E}}_ u N_i\le frac{T}{K-1}\). Instance \( u'\) raises arm \(i\) to \(2\Delta\). Divergence decomposition Divergence decomposition for bandits: \({\mathrm{KL}}={\mathbb{E}}_ u[N_i] frac{(2\Delta)^2}{2}\). Bretagnolle–Huber Bretagnolle–Huber inequality on the event \(\{N_1\le T/2\}\) then gives \({\mathrm{Reg}}_ u+{\mathrm{Reg}}_{ u'}\ge frac{T\Delta}{4}\exp(- frac{2T\Delta^2}{K-1})\); take \(\Delta=\sqrt{(K-1)/(4T)}\).
cards.ex: With \(K=10\), \(T=10^6\): no algorithm can guarantee regret below \(\approx110\) on all instances.
cards.use: Minimax optimality of algorithms, template for RL and non-stationary lower bounds.

cards.name: Doubling trick
cards.lay: If an algorithm needs to know the horizon \(T\) in advance, restart it on epochs of length \(1,2,4,\dots\); you lose only a constant factor in regret for \(\sqrt T\)-type bounds.
cards.st: If an algorithm tuned for horizon \(T'\) has regret \(\le C\sqrt{T'}\), running it on epochs of length \(2^m\), \(m=0,1,\dots\), gives for all \(T\): \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le\sum_{m=0}^{\lceil\log_2(T+1)\rceil-1}C\sqrt{2^m}\le\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt2-1}C\sqrt{T}\approx3.41\,C\sqrt T. \]
ver: For \(\log T\)-type bounds the geometric doubling gives \(O(\log^2T)\); use instead \(T_m=2^{2^m}\) (squaring trick) to keep \(O(\log T)\).
Adaptive restarts on detected changes in non-stationary environments are doubling-like Blocking / restarting argument (Besbes–Gur–Zeevi).
cards.det: Geometric series Geometric series & discounted sums: \(\sum_{m<M}\sqrt{2^m}=\tfrac{2^{M/2}-1}{\sqrt2-1}\) and \(2^{M/2}\le\sqrt{2T}\).
cards.ex: Hedge with \(\eta=\sqrt{8\log N/T}\) needs \(T\); doubling gives anytime regret \(\le3.41\sqrt{\tfrac T2\log N}\) (or use \(\eta_t\propto1/\sqrt t\)).
cards.use: Anytime algorithms, unknown variation budgets (combined with bandits-over-bandits), parameter-free learning.

cards.name: EXP3 & importance-weighted loss estimators
cards.lay: In adversarial bandits you only see the loss of the arm you pulled. Dividing it by the probability you pulled it gives an unbiased estimate of the full loss vector, whose variance is controlled. Feed that to Hedge and you get \(O(\sqrt{KT\log K})\) regret.
cards.st: With \(\hat\ell_t(i)=\frac{\ell_t(i){\mathbf{1}}\{A_t=i\}}{p_t(i)}\): \({\mathbb{E}}_t[\hat\ell_t(i)]=\ell_t(i)\) and \({\mathbb{E}}_t\bigl[\sum_ip_t(i)\hat\ell_t(i)^2\bigr]=\sum_i\ell_t(i)^2\le K\). Exponential weights on \(\hat\ell\) with \(\eta=\sqrt{\tfrac{2\log K}{KT}}\) give \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le\sqrt{2KT\log K}. \]
ver: Implicit exploration (EXP3-IX): \(\hat\ell=\tfrac{\ell{\mathbf{1}}}{p+\gamma}\) gives high-probability bounds.
EXP4 for contextual bandits with \(N\) experts: \(\sqrt{2KT\log N}\).
Adversarial MDPs with bandit feedback: importance-weight by occupancy measures \(q_t(s,a)\) (UOB-REPS).
Tsallis-INF achieves \(O(\sqrt{KT})\) and best-of-both-worlds.
cards.det: Use the local-norm Hedge bound Exponential weights (Hedge) regret bound (valid since \(\hat\ell\ge0\)): \({\mathbb{E}}{\mathrm{Reg}}\le\tfrac{\log K}{\eta}+\tfrac\eta2\sum_t{\mathbb{E}}\sum_ip_t(i)\hat\ell_t(i)^2\le\tfrac{\log K}{\eta}+\tfrac{\eta KT}{2}\).
cards.ex: Non-stationary adversarial bandits: EXP3 with restarts or EXP3.S (fixed-share) achieves dynamic regret \({\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{KTS})\) against comparators with \(S\) switches Dynamic regret of online gradient descent.
cards.use: Adversarial bandits and MDPs, off-policy estimators, partial-information online learning, non-stationary bandits.

cards.name: Information-ratio analysis (Russo–Van Roy)
cards.lay: Bound Bayesian regret by comparing, each round, the squared expected regret to the information gained about the optimal action. If this ratio is bounded, total regret is at most \(\sqrt{\text{ratio}\times\text{entropy of }A^\star\times T}\).
cards.st: Let \(\Gamma_t=\frac{({\mathbb{E}}_t[\Delta_t])^2}{I_t(A^\star;(A_t,Y_t))}\). If \(\Gamma_t\le\bar\Gamma\) for all \(t\), then \[ {\mathbb{E}}{\mathrm{Reg}}_T\le\sqrt{\bar\Gamma\,H(A^\star)\,T}. \] For Thompson sampling: \(\bar\Gamma\le K/2\) (\(K\) arms), \(\bar\Gamma\le d/2\) (linear bandits).
ver: Information-directed sampling chooses the action distribution minimising \(\Gamma_t\) directly.
Extensions to RL (PSRL Bayesian regret, Lu & Van Roy) and to non-stationary environments (Min & Russo 2023: regret driven by entropy rate of the optimal action sequence).
cards.det: Proof: \({\mathbb{E}}{\mathrm{Reg}}_T=\sum_t{\mathbb{E}}{\mathbb{E}}_t[\Delta_t]\le\sum_t\sqrt{\bar\Gamma{\mathbb{E}} I_t}\le\sqrt{\bar\Gamma T\sum_t{\mathbb{E}} I_t}\) (Cauchy–Schwarz Cauchy–Schwarz inequality) and \(\sum_t{\mathbb{E}} I_t=I(A^\star;\mathcal H_T)\le H(A^\star)\) by the MI chain rule Entropy, mutual information & their chain rules.
cards.ex: \(K\)-armed Bernoulli bandit with Thompson sampling: Bayesian regret \(\le\sqrt{\tfrac12KT\log K}\).
cards.use: Thompson sampling and PSRL Bayesian regret, information-directed sampling, non-stationary Bayesian bandits.

cards.name: Measures of non-stationarity (variation budget, switches, path length)
cards.plain: Measures of non-stationarity (variation budget, switches, path length)
cards.lay: To get non-trivial guarantees you must limit how much the environment can change. Three standard budgets: total variation (how much it drifts in total), number of switches (how often it jumps), and comparator path length (how much the optimal decision moves).
cards.st: For mean rewards \(\mu_t\in{\mathbb{R}}^K\), \(t\le T\): \[ V_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}{\lVert \mu_{t+1}-\mu_t\rVert}_\infty,\qquad L_T=1+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}{\mathbf{1}}\{\mu_{t+1}\ne\mu_t\},\qquad P_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}{\lVert u_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}. \] For MDPs: \(B_r=\sum_t\max_{s,a}|r_{t+1}(s,a)-r_t(s,a)|\) and \(B_p=\sum_t\max_{s,a}{\lVert P_{t+1}(\cdot|s,a)-P_t(\cdot|s,a)\rVert}_1\).
ver: Dynamic regret: \({\mathrm{Reg}}^{\mathrm{dyn}}_T=\sum_t\bigl(\max_a\mu_t(a)-\mu_t(A_t)\bigr)\) (compares against the per-round optimum).
Relations: if rewards are in \([0,1]\), \(V_T\le L_T-1\); a \(V_T\)-budget allows many small changes, an \(L_T\)-budget few arbitrary ones.

Local budgets over a window \({\mathcal{I}}\): \(V_{\mathcal{I}}=\sum_{t\in{\mathcal{I}}}{\lVert \mu_{t+1}-\mu_t\rVert}_\infty\) — what enters block-wise analyses Blocking / restarting argument (Besbes–Gur–Zeevi).
Episodic MDPs: \(\Delta=\sum_k\sum_h({\lVert r^{k+1}_h-r^k_h\rVert}_\infty+{\lVert P^{k+1}_h-P^k_h\rVert}_{1,\infty})\).
cards.det: The minimax dynamic regret for \(K\)-armed bandits is \(\tilde\Theta\bigl((KV_T)^{1/3}T^{2/3}\bigr)\) under a variation budget and \(\tilde\Theta(\sqrt{KL_TT})\) under \(L_T\) switches. Algorithms that need not know \(V_T\) or \(L_T\) exist (bandit-over-bandit tuning, change detection, Wei & Luo's MASTER reduction for RL).
cards.ex: A reward that oscillates by \(\pm{\varepsilon}\) every round has \(V_T=2{\varepsilon} T\) but \(L_T=T\): small variation, many switches — variation-budget methods handle it, switch-based ones do not.
cards.use: Defining the problem class in non-stationary bandits/MDPs, choosing the right algorithm family, stating dynamic-regret results.

cards.name: Drift-to-value lemma (sensitivity of values to environment change)
cards.plain: Drift-to-value lemma (sensitivity of values to environment change)
cards.lay: How much can a policy's value (or the optimal value) change if rewards and transitions drift a little? By the simulation lemma: by at most (reward drift)/(1-\(\gamma\)) + (transition drift)/(1-\(\gamma\))\(^2\). This converts environment drift into value drift.
cards.st: For MDPs \(M_t=(P_t,r_t)\), \(M_{t'}=(P_{t'},r_{t'})\) with rewards in \([0,1]\) and any \(\pi\): \[ {\lVert V^\pi_{M_t}-V^\pi_{M_{t'}}\rVert}_\infty\le\frac{{\lVert r_t-r_{t'}\rVert}_\infty}{1-\gamma}+\frac{\gamma\max_{s,a}{\lVert P_t(\cdot|s,a)-P_{t'}(\cdot|s,a)\rVert}_1}{(1-\gamma)^2}, \] and the same bound holds for \(|V^\star_{M_t}-V^\star_{M_{t'}}|\). Finite horizon: \(|V^\pi_{1,M}-V^\pi_{1,M'}|\le\sum_h{\lVert r_h-r'_h\rVert}_\infty+H\sum_h{\lVert P_h-P'_h\rVert}_{1,\infty}\).
ver: Telescoped over a block \({\mathcal{I}}\): \(\max_{t,t'\in{\mathcal{I}}}{\lVert V^\pi_{M_t}-V^\pi_{M_{t'}}\rVert}_\infty\le\tfrac{B_{r,{\mathcal{I}}}}{1-\gamma}+\tfrac{\gamma B_{p,{\mathcal{I}}}}{(1-\gamma)^2}\) (triangle inequality Triangle inequality (and its reverse)).
Optimal policy of the block-start MDP is near-optimal throughout the block: suboptimality \(\le2\times\) the above (cf. Greedy-policy loss bound (Singh–Yee; Williams–Baird)).
Q-function version and span-based version for average reward (replace \(\tfrac{1}{1-\gamma}\) by \({\operatorname{sp}}(h)\)).
cards.det: This is literally the simulation lemma Simulation lemma (model error \(\to\) value error) with \(\widehat M=M_{t'}\); the optimal-value version uses non-expansiveness of \(\max\) Non-expansiveness of \(\max\) / \(\sup\). In regret proofs it bounds the “drift cost” of using a single (stale) model or policy for a whole block or window.
cards.ex: Restart-based Q-learning with epochs of \(K_0\) episodes: within epoch \(j\) with local budget \(\Delta_j\), the optimal values move by at most \(H\Delta_j\), so the extra regret from non-stationarity in that epoch is \(\le K_0H\Delta_j\).
cards.use: Dynamic regret of restart/sliding-window RL algorithms (SWUCRL2-CW, Restart-Q-UCB), robust RL, sensitivity analysis.

cards.name: Blocking / restarting argument (Besbes–Gur–Zeevi)
cards.lay: Chop time into blocks, run a standard algorithm afresh in each block, and compare against the best fixed action within each block. Total regret = (static regret per block) \(\times\) (number of blocks) + (drift cost within blocks). Balancing block length gives \(T^{2/3}\) rates.
cards.st: With blocks of length \(\Delta\) and a base algorithm with static regret \(\le C\sqrt{\Delta}\) per block: \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}^{\mathrm{dyn}}_T\le\frac{T}{\Delta}C\sqrt{\Delta}+2\Delta V_T. \] Choosing \(\Delta\asymp(C/V_T)^{2/3}T^{2/3}\) yields \({\mathrm{Reg}}^{\mathrm{dyn}}_T=O\bigl(C^{2/3}V_T^{1/3}T^{2/3}\bigr)\); with EXP3 (\(C\asymp\sqrt{K\log K}\)) this is \(O\bigl((K\log K\,V_T)^{1/3}T^{2/3}\bigr)\).
ver: Drift cost lemma: in a block \({\mathcal{I}}\), \(\sum_{t\in{\mathcal{I}}}\max_a\mu_t(a)-\max_a\sum_{t\in{\mathcal{I}}}\mu_t(a)\le2|{\mathcal{I}}|V_{\mathcal{I}}\).
Switch budget: restart at (unknown) change points — with change detection, \({\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{KL_TT})\).
MDPs: Restart-Q-UCB / restarted UCBVI achieve \({\widetilde{O}}(\mathrm{poly}(S,A,H)\,\Delta^{1/3}T^{2/3})\) (e.g. Mao et al. 2021 for model-free).
Unknown \(V_T\): tune \(\Delta\) online with a bandit-over-bandits master (Cheung et al.) or use MASTER (Wei & Luo 2021) to get the optimal rate adaptively.
cards.det: Drift-cost proof: for \(t\in{\mathcal{I}}\) and any \(a\), \(|\mu_t(a)-\mu_{t_0}(a)|\le V_{\mathcal{I}}\); the per-round optimum differs from the block-fixed optimum by at most \(2V_{\mathcal{I}}\). The balancing step is AM–GM AM–GM inequality: minimise \(aT/\sqrt\Delta+b\Delta\).
cards.ex: \(K=10\), \(T=10^6\), \(V_T=10\): block length \(\Delta\approx(\sqrt{K\log K}/V_T)^{2/3}T^{2/3}\approx(0.48)^{2/3}10^4\approx6100\); regret \(\approx(K\log K\cdot V_T)^{1/3}T^{2/3}\approx6.1\times10^4\), sublinear but far above the stationary \(\sqrt{KT}\approx3200\).
cards.use: Rexp3, restarted UCB/Q-learning in drifting MDPs, analysing periodic retraining in deployed RL systems.

cards.name: Sliding-window & discounted estimators: bias–variance trade-off
cards.lay: Estimate the current mean using only the last \(\tau\) observations (or exponentially down-weighted past). A short window tracks changes (low bias) but is noisy (high variance); a long one is the opposite. The optimal window balances drift against noise.
cards.st: For a window of size \(\tau\) ending at \(t\) with \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise, with probability \(\ge1-\delta\): \[ \Bigl|\frac1\tau\sum_{s=t-\tau+1}^{t}X_s-\mu_t\Bigr|\le\underbrace{V_{[t-\tau,t]}}_{\text{bias (drift)}}+\underbrace{\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\delta)}{\tau}}}_{\text{variance}}. \] Under a total variation budget the optimal window is \(\tau\asymp(T/V_T)^{2/3}\), giving \(T^{2/3}V_T^{1/3}\)-type dynamic regret.
ver: Sliding-window UCB (Garivier & Moulines 2011): with \(L_T\) breakpoints and \(\tau\asymp\sqrt{T\log T/L_T}\), regret \({\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{KL_TT})\).

Discounted estimators with factor \(\beta<1\): effective sample size \(\approx\tfrac{1}{1-\beta}\); bias from data older than \(\approx\tfrac{\log(1/{\varepsilon})}{1-\beta}\) steps is \(\le{\varepsilon}\) Geometric series & discounted sums.

Weighted ridge regression for non-stationary linear bandits (D-LinUCB, SW-LinUCB): self-normalised bounds with weights Self-normalised bound for vector martingales (Abbasi-Yadkori et al.) and weighted elliptical potentials Elliptical potential lemma.
Sliding-window model estimates in MDPs (SWUCRL2-CW, Cheung et al. 2020) plus confidence widening.
cards.det:
Decomposition: estimate \(-\mu_t=(\text{average of }\mu_s-\mu_t)+(\text{average noise})\), triangle inequality Triangle inequality (and its reverse) (or Minkowski Minkowski's inequality for MSE), Hoeffding Hoeffding's inequality for the noise term. The bias term is bounded by the local variation since \(|\mu_s-\mu_t|\le V_{[s,t]}\).

Subtlety in bandits: the number of samples of an arm inside the window is random and can be small; analyses use a union bound over window counts and the pigeonhole lemma restricted to windows.
cards.ex: Tracking a mean drifting linearly at rate \(v\) per step with unit noise: MSE \(\approx(v\tau/2)^2+1/\tau\), minimised at \(\tau\approx(2/v^2)^{1/3}\), giving MSE \(\propto v^{2/3}\).
cards.use: SW-UCB, D-UCB, SW-LinUCB, D-LinUCB, SWUCRL2-CW, drifting parameter tracking in non-stationary MDPs.

cards.name: Dynamic regret of online gradient descent
cards.plain: Dynamic regret of online gradient descent
cards.lay: Online gradient descent can also track a moving target: its regret against an arbitrary sequence of comparators grows with how far that sequence travels (its path length). With a tuned step size the bound is \(\sqrt{T(1+P_T)}\).
cards.st: (Zinkevich 2003; Zhang, Lu, Zhou 2018) For convex \(G\)-Lipschitz losses on a domain of diameter \(D\), OGD with fixed step \(\eta\) satisfies for any comparators \(u_1,\dots,u_T\): \[ \sum_tf_t(x_t)-\sum_tf_t(u_t)\le\frac{7D^2+4DP_T}{4\eta}+\frac{\eta G^2T}{2},\qquad P_T=\sum_{t}{\lVert u_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}. \] With \(\eta\asymp\sqrt{D(D+P_T)/(G^2T)}\): \(O\bigl(\sqrt{T(1+P_T)}\bigr)\), which is minimax optimal.
ver: Unknown \(P_T\): run OGD with a grid of step sizes and combine with Hedge (Ader, Zhang et al. 2018) — \(O(\sqrt{T(1+P_T)})\) adaptively.

Strongly convex / smooth losses: bounds in terms of \(P_T\), squared path length \(S_T\), or functional variation \(V_T^f=\sum_t\sup_x|f_{t+1}(x)-f_t(x)|\) (\(O(T^{2/3}(V_T^f)^{1/3})\), Besbes, Gur & Zeevi 2015).
Experts with \(S\) switches: fixed-share Hedge achieves \({\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{TS\log N})\) (Herbster & Warmuth).
Adaptive (strongly adaptive) regret on every interval \(\Rightarrow\) dynamic regret (Daniely et al. 2015).
cards.det: Proof: as in static OGD Online gradient descent regret (Zinkevich), but the telescoping \(\tfrac{1}{2\eta}({\lVert x_t-u_t\rVert}^2-{\lVert x_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}^2)\) no longer cancels exactly; correcting \({\lVert x_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}^2\to{\lVert x_{t+1}-u_{t+1}\rVert}^2\) costs \(\le\tfrac{1}{2\eta}\cdot2D{\lVert u_{t+1}-u_t\rVert}\) each round, summing to the path-length term.
cards.ex: Tracking a drifting Lagrange multiplier in a non-stationary constrained MDP: dual dynamic regret scales with how much the optimal multiplier moves.
cards.use: Non-stationary online learning, policy optimisation in drifting MDPs (per-state OMD with path-length bounds), tracking problems.

cards.name: Lower bounds for non-stationary bandits & MDPs
cards.plain: Lower bounds for non-stationary bandits & MDPs
cards.lay: You cannot beat \(T^{2/3}V_T^{1/3}\) (variation budget) or \(\sqrt{L_TT}\) (switch budget): the environment can change exactly when you have just finished learning it. Proved by gluing stationary hard instances in blocks.
cards.st: (Besbes, Gur & Zeevi 2014) For every policy there is a \(K\)-armed environment with variation \(\le V_T\) such that \[ {\mathrm{Reg}}^{\mathrm{dyn}}_T\ge c\,(KV_T)^{1/3}T^{2/3}. \] With \(L_T\) abrupt changes: \({\mathrm{Reg}}^{\mathrm{dyn}}_T\ge c\sqrt{KL_TT}\) (Garivier & Moulines 2011).
ver: Episodic MDPs with total variation budget \(\Delta\): lower bounds of order \(\Delta^{1/3}T^{2/3}\) times polynomial factors in \(S,A,H\) (Mao et al. 2021).
Linear bandits: \(\Omega(d^{2/3}V_T^{1/3}T^{2/3})\) (Cheung, Simchi-Levi & Zhu).
cards.det: Construction: split \([T]\) into blocks of length \(\Delta\); in each block independently pick a uniformly random arm to be better by \({\varepsilon}\). Total variation \(\approx\tfrac{T}{\Delta}{\varepsilon}\le V_T\). Within a block, the stationary minimax bound Minimax \(\Omega(\sqrt{KT})\) lower bound gives regret \(\gtrsim\min({\varepsilon}\Delta,\sqrt{K\Delta})\); choose \({\varepsilon}\asymp\sqrt{K/\Delta}\) and \(\Delta\asymp(K^{1/2}T/V_T)^{2/3}\).
cards.ex: These lower bounds show the restarting upper bound Blocking / restarting argument (Besbes–Gur–Zeevi) is optimal up to \((\log K)^{1/3}\).
cards.use: Certifying optimality of non-stationary algorithms; motivating structural assumptions (e.g. smooth drift, periodicity) to beat \(T^{2/3}\).

cards.name: Change detection: CUSUM / GLR delay–false-alarm trade-off
cards.plain: Change detection: CUSUM / GLR delay–false-alarm trade-off
cards.lay: To detect a change in a data stream, accumulate log-likelihood ratios and raise an alarm when the running total (reset at zero) crosses a threshold \(b\). False alarms are exponentially rare in \(b\); detection takes about \(b/{\mathrm{KL}}\) samples after the change.
cards.st: CUSUM for known pre/post-change densities \(p_0,p_1\): \(W_t=\max(0,W_{t-1}+\log\tfrac{p_1(X_t)}{p_0(X_t)})\), alarm when \(W_t\ge b\). Then the average run length to false alarm is \(\ge e^b\) and the worst-case expected detection delay satisfies \[ \mathrm{EDD}\sim\frac{b}{{\mathrm{KL}}(p_1\|p_0)}\quad(b\to\infty), \] which is optimal (Lorden 1971; Moustakides 1986).
ver: Unknown post-change parameter: GLR (generalised likelihood ratio) statistics; for bounded/sub-Gaussian means use the Bernoulli GLR test (Besson et al. 2022) with thresholds \(\approx\log(t^{3/2}/\delta)\).
Bandit integration: CUSUM-UCB, M-UCB, GLR-klUCB achieve \({\widetilde{O}}(\sqrt{KL_TT})\) with forced exploration.
Ville-based (anytime-valid) change detectors via e-processes Ville's inequality & method of mixtures (time-uniform bounds).
cards.det: Under no change, \(e^{W}\)-type statistics are controlled by non-negative supermartingales (likelihood ratios under \(p_0\)), hence Ville Ville's inequality & method of mixtures (time-uniform bounds) bounds false alarms. After the change, \(\log\tfrac{p_1}{p_0}\) has mean \({\mathrm{KL}}(p_1\|p_0)\), so the walk drifts upward at that rate (Wald Wald's identity).
cards.ex: Bernoulli rewards jumping from \(0.5\) to \(0.7\): \({\mathrm{KL}}(p_1\|p_0)\approx0.082\); with \(b=\log(10^4)\approx9.2\), detection takes \(\approx112\) samples on average, with false alarms roughly once every \(10^4\) steps.
cards.use: Adaptive restarts in non-stationary bandits/RL, monitoring deployed policies, piecewise-stationary environments.

cards.name: ELBO decomposition (free-energy view of EM)
cards.lay: For any guess \(q\) of the hidden variables' distribution, the log-likelihood splits into a lower bound (the ELBO) plus the KL gap between \(q\) and the true posterior. EM alternately closes the gap (E-step: set \(q\) to the posterior) and pushes up the bound (M-step).
cards.st: For latent-variable model \(p_\theta(x,z)\) and any distribution \(q(z)\): \[ \log p_\theta(x)=\underbrace{{\mathbb{E}}_{q}\bigl[\log p_\theta(x,z)\bigr]+H(q)}_{F(q,\theta)\ (\text{ELBO})}+{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(q(z)\,\|\,p_\theta(z\mid x)\bigr)\ \ge\ F(q,\theta). \] EM is coordinate ascent on \(F\) (Neal & Hinton 1998): E-step \(q_{t+1}=p_{\theta_t}(\cdot\mid x)\); M-step \(\theta_{t+1}={\operatorname*{arg\,max}}_\theta{\mathbb{E}}_{q_{t+1}}\log p_\theta(x,z)={\operatorname*{arg\,max}}_\theta Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)\).
ver: Jensen form: \(\log p_\theta(x)=\log{\mathbb{E}}_q\tfrac{p_\theta(x,z)}{q(z)}\ge{\mathbb{E}}_q\log\tfrac{p_\theta(x,z)}{q(z)}\) Jensen's inequality.
Gibbs-variational form: \(\log p_\theta(x)=\max_qF(q,\theta)\), maximiser \(=\) posterior Donsker–Varadhan & Gibbs variational principle.
Variational EM / VI: restrict \(q\) to a tractable family \(\Rightarrow\) only a lower bound is maximised.
Incremental / online EM: partial E-steps still increase \(F\), giving convergence of incremental variants.
cards.det:
Verification: \(\log p_\theta(x)=\log p_\theta(x,z)-\log p_\theta(z|x)\) for every \(z\); average over \(q\) and add/subtract \(\log q(z)\).

Because \(F(q,\theta)\) is a single objective, EM inherits all coordinate-ascent intuition: monotonicity Monotonicity of EM (and GEM), fixed points are stationary points of \(\log p_\theta(x)\) (envelope theorem Danskin's theorem / envelope theorem), and generalised/partial steps still work.
cards.ex: Gaussian mixture: E-step responsibilities \(\gamma_{ik}=\tfrac{\pi_k{\mathcal{N}}(x_i;\mu_k,\Sigma_k)}{\sum_j\pi_j{\mathcal{N}}(x_i;\mu_j,\Sigma_j)}\); M-step weighted MLEs \(\mu_k=\tfrac{\sum_i\gamma_{ik}x_i}{\sum_i\gamma_{ik}}\), \(\pi_k=\tfrac1n\sum_i\gamma_{ik}\).
cards.use: Deriving and analysing EM, variational inference, RL-as-inference (MPO, reward-weighted regression, V-MPO), latent-mode inference in non-stationary MDPs, HMM/Baum–Welch.

cards.name: Monotonicity of EM (and GEM)
cards.lay: Each EM iteration never decreases the observed-data likelihood. Any update that merely increases the \(Q\)-function (generalised EM) has the same guarantee.
cards.st: If \(Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)\) where \(Q(\theta\mid\theta')={\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim p_{\theta'}(\cdot|x)}[\log p_\theta(x,z)]\), then \[ \log p_{\theta_{t+1}}(x)-\log p_{\theta_t}(x)\ge Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)-Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)\ge0. \]
ver: Exact gap: \(\log p_{\theta}(x)-\log p_{\theta_t}(x)=Q(\theta|\theta_t)-Q(\theta_t|\theta_t)+{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(p_{\theta_t}(\cdot|x)\|p_\theta(\cdot|x)\bigr)\).
MM interpretation: \(g(\theta|\theta_t)=Q(\theta|\theta_t)+H(p_{\theta_t}(\cdot|x))\) is a minorant of \(\log p_\theta(x)\) tight at \(\theta_t\) EM as minorise–maximise and as mirror descent.
Monotonicity does not imply convergence to a global maximum (local maxima, saddle points) — see Wu's convergence theorem for EM.
cards.det: Proof: from the ELBO decomposition ELBO decomposition (free-energy view of EM) with \(q=p_{\theta_t}(\cdot|x)\): \(\log p_\theta(x)\ge F(q,\theta)=Q(\theta|\theta_t)+H(q)\), with equality at \(\theta=\theta_t\). So \(\log p_{\theta_{t+1}}(x)\ge Q(\theta_{t+1}|\theta_t)+H(q)\ge Q(\theta_t|\theta_t)+H(q)=\log p_{\theta_t}(x)\).
cards.ex: Even if the M-step is only one gradient ascent step on \(Q\) (gradient EM Gradient EM & first-order EM variants), likelihood is non-decreasing for small enough steps (GEM).
cards.use: Sanity checks for EM implementations, convergence proofs, designing GEM/ECM variants in complex RL models.

cards.name: Fisher's identity (score of the observed likelihood)
cards.plain: Fisher's identity (score of the observed likelihood)
cards.lay: The gradient of the observed-data log-likelihood equals the posterior average of the complete-data gradient. You can compute likelihood gradients without ever marginalising — and at the current parameter, the gradient of EM's \(Q\)-function is the true score.
cards.st: Under regularity conditions: \[ abla_ heta\log p_ heta(x)={\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim p_ heta(\cdot|x)} igl[ abla_ heta\log p_ heta(x,z) igr]= abla_{ heta'}Q( heta'\mid heta) ig|_{ heta'= heta}. \]
ver: Consequence: fixed points of EM (\(\theta=M(\theta)\) with interior M-step) are stationary points of the likelihood.
Policy-gradient analogue: \(\nabla\log p_\theta(\tau)=\sum_t\nabla\log\pi_\theta(a_t|s_t)\), dynamics marginalised Log-derivative (score-function) trick & differentiating under the integral.
Second-order: Louis' identity for the observed information Missing-information principle (Louis) & EM's convergence rate.
cards.det: Proof: \( abla\log p_ heta(x)= frac{\int abla p_ heta(x,z){\mathrm{d}} z}{p_ heta(x)}=\int frac{p_ heta(x,z)}{p_ heta(x)} abla\log p_ heta(x,z){\mathrm{d}} z\) by the log-derivative trick Log-derivative (score-function) trick & differentiating under the integral.
cards.ex: HMMs: the gradient of the log-likelihood is a sum over time of posterior-weighted complete-data gradients, computable with forward–backward — the basis of gradient-based training of HMM-modulated (latent-mode) MDP models.
cards.use: Gradient EM and stochastic-gradient EM, MCMC-EM, likelihood gradients in latent MDP models, showing EM fixed points are stationary.

cards.name: Missing-information principle (Louis) & EM's convergence rate
cards.lay: Observed information = complete information \(-\) missing information. EM's local convergence rate equals the fraction of information that is missing: lots of latent uncertainty means slow EM.
cards.st: At \( heta\), with \(I_c={\mathbb{E}}[- abla^2\log p_ heta(x,z)\mid x]\) and \(I_m={\operatorname{Cov}} igl( abla\log p_ heta(x,z)\mid x igr)={\mathbb{E}}[- abla^2\log p_ heta(z\mid x)\mid x]\): \[ I_{\mathrm{obs}}( heta)=- abla^2\log p_ heta(x)=I_c( heta)-I_m( heta). \] (Dempster, Laird & Rubin 1977) Near a local maximum \( heta^\star\), the EM map has Jacobian \(DM( heta^\star)=I_c^{-1}I_m=I-I_c^{-1}I_{\mathrm{obs}}\), so the linear rate is its spectral radius \( ho(I_c^{-1}I_m)<1\).
ver: Rate interpretation: eigenvalues of \(I_c^{-1}I_m\) are the “fractions of missing information” in each direction.
Acceleration: Aitken/SQUAREM, PX-EM, ECME exploit the rate formula.
Standard errors for EM estimates: SEM algorithm (Meng & Rubin) estimates \(DM\) numerically to recover \(I_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
cards.det: Differentiate Fisher's identity Fisher's identity (score of the observed likelihood) once more to get Louis' formula. Differentiating the fixed-point equation \( abla_1Q(M( heta)| heta)=0\) by the implicit function theorem Implicit & inverse function theorems gives \(DM=[- abla_{11}Q]^{-1} abla_{12}Q\), and at \( heta^\star\) these blocks are \(I_c\) and \(I_m\).
cards.ex: Two-component Gaussian mixture with heavily overlapping components: posteriors are near \(\tfrac12\), \(I_m\approx I_c\), rate near \(1\) — EM crawls. Well-separated components: \(I_m\approx0\), EM converges in a few steps (consistent with Balakrishnan–Wainwright–Yu: population EM contraction).
cards.use: Predicting/diagnosing slow EM, standard errors, choosing between EM and Newton/gradient methods, latent-mode MDP identification difficulty.

cards.name: Wu's convergence theorem for EM
cards.lay: Under mild continuity and compactness conditions, every limit point of EM (or generalised EM) is a stationary point of the likelihood, and the likelihood values converge. It does not promise a global maximum.
cards.st: (Wu 1983, via Zangwill's global convergence theorem) Suppose \(\Omega\) is the parameter set, \(\{\theta:\log p_\theta(x)\ge\log p_{\theta_0}(x)\}\) is compact, \(\log p_\theta(x)\) is continuous on \(\Omega\) and differentiable in its interior, and \(Q(\theta\mid\theta')\) is continuous in both arguments. Then all limit points of a GEM sequence are stationary points of \(\log p_\theta(x)\), and \(\log p_{\theta_t}(x)\) converges monotonically to \(\log p_{\theta^\star}(x)\) for some stationary \(\theta^\star\).
ver: Convergence of the iterates themselves (not only of likelihood values) needs more, e.g. isolated stationary points or \({\lVert \theta_{t+1}-\theta_t\rVert}\to0\).
Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz arguments give iterate convergence for analytic likelihoods.
cards.det: Zangwill: a descent algorithm with a closed point-to-set map and a continuous Lyapunov function (here \(-\log p_\theta(x)\)) on a compact set has all limit points in the solution set. Monotonicity Monotonicity of EM (and GEM) supplies the Lyapunov property.
cards.ex: Mixtures with a component collapsing onto one data point (\(\sigma\to0\)) violate compactness — likelihood is unbounded and EM can diverge; constraining \(\sigma\ge\sigma_{\min}\) restores Wu's conditions.
cards.use: Qualitative convergence guarantees, checking assumptions for EM-based RL models, justifying constraints/regularisation.

cards.name: Balakrishnan–Wainwright–Yu: population EM contraction
cards.lay: Analyse EM in two steps. (1) The idealised “population” EM operator (infinite data) is a contraction in a ball around the true parameter if the \(Q\)-function is strongly concave and its gradient is stable in its second argument. (2) Finite-sample EM stays close to population EM uniformly on that ball. Together: geometric convergence up to statistical error.
cards.st: Let \(M(\theta)={\operatorname*{arg\,max}}_{\theta'}Q(\theta'|\theta)\) (population). Assume on a ball \(B=\{{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert}\le r\}\): \(Q(\cdot|\theta^\star)\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly concave, and first-order stability (FOS) holds: \({\lVert \nabla Q(M(\theta)|\theta^\star)-\nabla Q(M(\theta)|\theta)\rVert}\le\gamma{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert}\). If \(\gamma<\lambda\), then for \(\theta\in B\): \[ {\lVert M(\theta)-\theta^\star\rVert}\le\kappa{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert},\qquad\kappa=\frac\gamma\lambda<1. \] Sample EM: if \(\sup_{\theta\in B}{\lVert M_n(\theta)-M(\theta)\rVert}\le{\varepsilon}_n(\delta)\) w.p. \(\ge1-\delta\), then \({\lVert \theta_t-\theta^\star\rVert}\le\kappa^t{\lVert \theta_0-\theta^\star\rVert}+\frac{{\varepsilon}_n(\delta)}{1-\kappa}\).
ver: Gradient EM: \(\theta^+=\theta+\alpha\nabla Q(\theta|\theta)\) with \(Q(\cdot|\theta^\star)\) \(\lambda\)-strongly concave and \(\mu\)-smooth and gradient stability \(\gamma\): with \(\alpha=\tfrac{2}{\mu+\lambda}\), contraction factor \(1-\tfrac{2(\lambda-\gamma)}{\mu+\lambda}\) Gradient EM & first-order EM variants.

Symmetric 2-GMM \(\tfrac12{\mathcal{N}}(\theta^\star,\sigma^2I)+\tfrac12{\mathcal{N}}(-\theta^\star,\sigma^2I)\) with large SNR \(\eta={\lVert \theta^\star\rVert}/\sigma\): \(\kappa\le e^{-c\eta^2}\) on \(B(\theta^\star,{\lVert \theta^\star\rVert}/4)\), statistical error \({\varepsilon}_n\lesssim\sigma\sqrt{d\log(1/\delta)/n}\) (up to SNR factors).
Sample splitting variant (fresh batch each iteration) needs only pointwise, not uniform, deviation bounds.
High-dimensional (sparse) EM: truncation step plus restricted strong concavity (Wang et al. 2015; Yi & Caramanis 2015).
Low-SNR / overspecified mixtures: contraction fails, EM is sublinear, with rates \(n^{-1/4}\) or slower (Dwivedi et al. 2020).
cards.det:
Population proof: optimality of \(M(\theta)\) for \(Q(\cdot|\theta)\) and of \(\theta^\star=M(\theta^\star)\) (self-consistency) for \(Q(\cdot|\theta^\star)\); strong concavity gives \(\lambda{\lVert M(\theta)-\theta^\star\rVert}^2\le{\langle \nabla Q(M(\theta)|\theta^\star)-\nabla Q(M(\theta)|\theta), M(\theta)-\theta^\star\rangle}\), and FOS bounds the right side by \(\gamma{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert}{\lVert M(\theta)-\theta^\star\rVert}\).

Sample analysis: triangle inequality \({\lVert M_n(\theta_t)-\theta^\star\rVert}\le{\lVert M_n(\theta_t)-M(\theta_t)\rVert}+\kappa{\lVert \theta_t-\theta^\star\rVert}\) and unroll the recursion (geometric series Geometric series & discounted sums). The uniform deviation \({\varepsilon}_n\) is obtained by empirical-process tools (symmetrisation, covering Covering & packing numbers (volumetric bound)).
cards.ex: Mixture of two regressions \(y=\pm{\langle x, \beta^\star\rangle}+{\varepsilon}\): with SNR above a constant and initialisation within \({\lVert \beta^\star\rVert}/32\), EM converges geometrically to within \({\widetilde{O}}(\sigma\sqrt{d/n})\) of \(\beta^\star\).
cards.use: Finite-sample EM guarantees (GMMs, mixed regression, missing data), template for analysing EM inside RL (latent-context MDPs, mixture-of-MDPs, regime-switching environments), sample complexity of EM-based policy improvement.

cards.name: Inexact contraction lemma (sample/stochastic EM, inexact fixed-point iterations)
cards.plain: Inexact contraction lemma (sample/stochastic EM, inexact fixed-point iterations)
cards.lay: If an exact iteration contracts by \(\kappa\) and each actual step makes an error at most \({\varepsilon}\), iterates converge geometrically to within \({\varepsilon}/(1-\kappa)\) of the fixed point. The skeleton behind sample-EM, approximate VI and stochastic fixed-point methods alike.
cards.st: If \({\lVert M(\theta)-\theta^\star\rVert}\le\kappa{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert}\) on \(B\) with \(\kappa<1\), and the implemented update satisfies \({\lVert \widehat M_t(\theta_t)-M(\theta_t)\rVert}\le{\varepsilon}_t\) with iterates staying in \(B\), then \[ {\lVert \theta_T-\theta^\star\rVert}\le\kappa^T{\lVert \theta_0-\theta^\star\rVert}+\sum_{t<T}\kappa^{T-1-t}{\varepsilon}_t\le\kappa^T{\lVert \theta_0-\theta^\star\rVert}+\frac{\max_t{\varepsilon}_t}{1-\kappa}. \]
ver: Staying in the ball: guaranteed if \(\kappa r+\max_t{\varepsilon}_t\le r\).
Decaying errors (growing batches): if \({\varepsilon}_t\le c\rho^t\) with \(\rho\ne\kappa\), the error decays like \(\max(\kappa,\rho)^T\).
Same lemma gives approximate value iteration Value iteration convergence & stopping rules (with \(\kappa=\gamma\)).
Stochastic EM / online EM (Cappé & Moulines 2009) instead uses Robbins–Monro averaging of sufficient statistics Robbins–Monro stochastic approximation.
cards.det: Proof by induction with the triangle inequality Triangle inequality (and its reverse): \({\lVert \theta_{t+1}-\theta^\star\rVert}\le{\lVert \widehat M_t(\theta_t)-M(\theta_t)\rVert}+{\lVert M(\theta_t)-\theta^\star\rVert}\le{\varepsilon}_t+\kappa{\lVert \theta_t-\theta^\star\rVert}\), then the geometric recursion Geometric series & discounted sums.
cards.ex: With \(\kappa=0.5\) and per-step statistical error \({\varepsilon}=0.01\), \(T=10\) iterations from distance \(1\) reach \(\approx0.001+0.02=0.021\); further iterations cannot beat \(0.02\).
cards.use: Sample EM, Monte-Carlo EM, approximate DP, inexact policy evaluation inside EM-based policy optimisation.

cards.name: Gradient EM & first-order EM variants
cards.lay: Replace the (possibly intractable) M-step by one gradient step on the \(Q\)-function. By Fisher's identity this is gradient ascent on the log-likelihood itself, so smooth-optimisation theory applies directly, and local contraction holds under BWY-type conditions.
cards.st: Gradient EM: \( heta_{t+1}= heta_t+\alpha abla_1Q( heta_t\mid heta_t)= heta_t+\alpha abla\log p_{ heta_t}(x)\). If \(Q(\cdot| heta^\star)\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly concave and \(\mu\)-smooth on \(B\) and gradient stability \({\lVert abla_1Q( heta| heta^\star)- abla_1Q( heta| heta) Vert}\le\gamma{\lVert heta- heta^\star Vert}\) holds with \(\gamma<\lambda\), then with \(\alpha= frac{2}{\mu+\lambda}\): \[ {\lVert heta_{t+1}- heta^\star Vert}\le\Bigl(1- rac{2(\lambda-\gamma)}{\mu+\lambda}\Bigr){\lVert heta_t- heta^\star Vert}. \]
ver: Stochastic gradient EM / online EM: unbiased minibatch estimates of \(\nabla_1Q\), analysed like SGD Stochastic gradient descent convergence.
ECM: conditional maximisation over blocks of parameters (still GEM, monotone).
Natural-gradient view: for exponential families, EM equals a natural-gradient / mirror step EM as minorise–maximise and as mirror descent.
cards.det: Proof: one gradient step on the strongly concave, smooth \(Q(\cdot|\theta^\star)\) contracts by \(1-\tfrac{2\lambda}{\mu+\lambda}\) (standard GD analysis Strong convexity, PL & quadratic growth); the gradient-stability condition adds a perturbation \(\alpha\gamma{\lVert \theta-\theta^\star\rVert}\).
cards.ex: In latent-mode MDP learning where the M-step over transition models is a constrained problem, a projected gradient step on \(Q\) keeps monotonicity and the local linear rate.
cards.use: Large models where the M-step is expensive (neural likelihoods), streaming/online EM, combining EM with policy-gradient updates.

cards.name: EM as minorise–maximise and as mirror descent
cards.plain: EM as minorise–maximise and as mirror descent
cards.lay: EM is a special case of MM (minorise–maximise): it maximises a surrogate that touches the objective at the current point and lies below it everywhere. For exponential-family models, EM is exactly mirror descent with the KL/Bregman geometry, which yields non-asymptotic rates without strong concavity.
cards.st: (MM) \(g( heta| heta_t)=Q( heta| heta_t)+H(p_{ heta_t}(\cdot|x))\le\log p_ heta(x)\) with equality at \( heta_t\). (Kunstner, Kumar & Schmidt 2021) If the complete-data model is an exponential family with log-partition \(A\), then EM is mirror descent on \(-\log p_ heta(x)\) with mirror map \(A\) and unit step: \[ abla A( heta_{t+1})= abla A( heta_t)+ abla_ heta\log p_{ heta_t}(x), \] and \(-\log p_ heta(x)\) is \(1\)-smooth relative to \(A\), giving \(O(1/T)\) convergence of a KL-based stationarity measure.
ver: Relative smoothness/strong convexity framework (Bauschke, Bolte & Teboulle 2017; Lu, Freund & Nesterov 2018).
Linear convergence if additionally relatively strongly convex near the optimum.

Connection to RL: policy mirror descent/NPG Natural policy gradient & policy mirror descent convergence and EM-style RL (MPO, REPS) share the same KL-proximal structure Donsker–Varadhan & Gibbs variational principle.
cards.det: In the mean-parameter coordinates \(\nabla A(\theta)\), the M-step sets the expected sufficient statistics to their posterior averages, which is a mirror step. The three-point identity for the Bregman divergence of \(A\) Bregman divergences & the three-point identity then gives the standard mirror-descent descent inequality.
cards.ex: Gaussian mixtures with known covariances: EM's update of mixture weights is exactly entropic mirror descent on the simplex (multiplicative update), like Hedge Exponential weights (Hedge) regret bound.
cards.use: Non-asymptotic EM rates without local strong concavity; unifying EM with policy mirror descent and KL-regularised RL; designing EM-like updates in RL.

cards.name: Paley–Zygmund inequality (anti-concentration)
cards.lay: The reverse of Markov: a non-negative variable with a decent mean and not-too-large second moment exceeds a fraction of its mean with constant probability. Used to show that “good” events happen often enough (e.g. optimism with constant probability).
cards.st: For \(Z\ge0\) with finite variance and \(\theta\in[0,1]\): \[ \Pr\bigl(Z>\theta\,{\mathbb{E}} Z\bigr)\ge(1-\theta)^2\frac{({\mathbb{E}} Z)^2}{{\mathbb{E}} Z^2}. \]
ver: Second-moment method (\(\theta=0\)): \(\Pr(Z>0)\ge\tfrac{({\mathbb{E}} Z)^2}{{\mathbb{E}} Z^2}\).
Cantelli-improved form: \(\Pr(Z>\theta{\mathbb{E}} Z)\ge\tfrac{(1-\theta)^2({\mathbb{E}} Z)^2}{{\operatorname{Var}} Z+(1-\theta)^2({\mathbb{E}} Z)^2}\).
cards.det: Proof: \({\mathbb{E}} Z\le\theta{\mathbb{E}} Z+{\mathbb{E}}[Z{\mathbf{1}}\{Z>\theta{\mathbb{E}} Z\}]\le\theta{\mathbb{E}} Z+\sqrt{{\mathbb{E}} Z^2\Pr(Z>\theta{\mathbb{E}} Z)}\) by Cauchy–Schwarz Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
cards.ex: Randomised exploration (RLSVI-type): showing that a randomly perturbed value estimate is optimistic with constant probability can use Paley–Zygmund on the perturbation's projection.
cards.use: Anti-concentration in randomised exploration, lower bounds, random-graph connectivity.

cards.name: Efron–Stein inequality
cards.lay: The variance of any function of independent inputs is at most the sum over coordinates of how much the function changes when that coordinate is resampled. A variance analogue of McDiarmid that needs no boundedness.
cards.st: For independent \(X_1,\dots,X_n\), an independent copy \(X'_i\) of each, and \(Z=f(X_1,\dots,X_n)\), \(Z^{(i)}=f(X_1,..,X'_i,..,X_n)\): \[ {\operatorname{Var}}(Z)\le\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n{\mathbb{E}}\bigl[(Z-Z^{(i)})^2\bigr]. \]
ver: Bounded differences \(|Z-Z^{(i)}|\le c_i\): \({\operatorname{Var}} Z\le\tfrac12\sum c_i^2\).
Self-bounding functions get Bernstein-like concentration (Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart).
cards.det: Proof via the martingale (Doob) decomposition of \(Z-{\mathbb{E}} Z\) and Jensen on each increment.
cards.ex: Variance of the maximum of \(n\) i.i.d. variables or of the value of a randomly perturbed planning problem is controlled by the effect of resampling one input.
cards.use: Variance bounds for complex estimators, stability of learned policies to single-sample changes.

cards.name: Hanson–Wright inequality
cards.lay: Quadratic forms \(X^\top AX\) of a vector with independent sub-Gaussian entries concentrate around their mean, with a sub-Gaussian regime governed by the Frobenius norm and a sub-exponential regime governed by the operator norm.
cards.st: For \(X\in{\mathbb{R}}^n\) with independent mean-zero \(K\)-sub-Gaussian coordinates and fixed \(A\): \[ \Pr\bigl(|X^\top AX-{\mathbb{E}} X^\top AX|>t\bigr)\le2\exp\Bigl(-c\min\Bigl\{\frac{t^2}{K^4{\lVert A\rVert}_F^2},\frac{t}{K^2{\lVert A\rVert}_2}\Bigr\}\Bigr). \]
ver: Norm concentration: \(\bigl|{\lVert BX\rVert}_2-{\lVert B\rVert}_F\bigr|\) is \(O(K^2{\lVert B\rVert}_2)\)-sub-Gaussian.
cards.det: Decouple diagonal and off-diagonal parts; off-diagonal via decoupling and Gaussian comparison; diagonal via Bernstein for sub-exponential variables Sub-exponential variables & Bernstein condition.
cards.ex: Concentration of \({\lVert \hat\theta-\theta\rVert}_\Sigma^2\) for least squares with sub-Gaussian noise, a quadratic form in the noise vector.
cards.use: Least-squares error concentration, random features, high-dimensional linear RL analyses.

cards.name: Talagrand's convex-distance inequality
cards.lay: In a product space, the probability of being far (in a special “convex distance”) from a set of probability at least \(\tfrac12\) is exponentially small. Gives dimension-free concentration of convex Lipschitz functions of bounded independent variables.
cards.st: For a product probability \(P\) on \(\Omega^n\) and measurable \(A\): \[ P(A)\,\Pr\bigl(d_T(X,A)\ge t\bigr)\le e^{-t^2/4}, \] where \(d_T\) is Talagrand's convex distance. Consequence: for convex \(1\)-Lipschitz \(f:[0,1]^n\to{\mathbb{R}}\), \(\Pr(|f(X)-\mathrm{Med}f(X)|\ge t)\le4e^{-t^2/4}\).
ver: Talagrand's inequality for suprema of empirical processes (Bousquet's form): Bernstein-type concentration of \(\sup_f\sum_i(f(X_i)-{\mathbb{E}} f)\) with variance \(\sigma^2\).
cards.det: Bousquet's version underlies local Rademacher complexity and fast-rate analyses for regression-based RL (e.g. sharp FQI rates).
cards.ex: Largest eigenvalue of a random matrix with bounded independent entries concentrates around its median with \(O(1)\) fluctuations.
cards.use: Fast rates via localisation, random matrix concentration, combinatorial optimisation.

cards.name: Slepian / Sudakov–Fernique comparison & Sudakov minoration
cards.lay: Compare two Gaussian processes: if one has larger increments, its expected supremum is larger. Combined with Sudakov's minoration, this gives lower bounds on expected maxima — matching Dudley's upper bound up to logs.
cards.st: (Sudakov–Fernique) For centred Gaussian processes \(X,Y\) on \(T\) with \({\mathbb{E}}(X_s-X_t)^2\le{\mathbb{E}}(Y_s-Y_t)^2\) for all \(s,t\): \({\mathbb{E}}\sup_tX_t\le{\mathbb{E}}\sup_tY_t\). (Sudakov minoration) For all \({\varepsilon}>0\): \[ {\mathbb{E}}\sup_{t\in T}X_t\ge c\,{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\log N({\varepsilon},T,d_X)},\quad d_X(s,t)=\sqrt{{\mathbb{E}}(X_s-X_t)^2}. \]
ver: Slepian's lemma (equal variances, ordered covariances) compares probabilities of suprema.
Gordon's min–max comparison (behind Gaussian width bounds).
cards.det: Proof by Gaussian interpolation and Stein's lemma Stein's lemma (Gaussian integration by parts).
cards.ex: Lower bound \({\mathbb{E}}\max_{i\le n}Z_i\ge c\sqrt{\log n}\) for i.i.d. Gaussians follows from Sudakov with \({\varepsilon}=\sqrt2\).
cards.use: Lower bounds on suprema, Gaussian bandit lower bounds, compressed sensing-style arguments.

cards.name: Stein's lemma (Gaussian integration by parts)
cards.lay: For a Gaussian \(Z\), \({\mathbb{E}}[Zg(Z)]={\mathbb{E}}[g'(Z)]\). Lets you move derivatives onto test functions, compute gradients of Gaussian expectations, and characterise normality.
cards.st: If \(Z\sim{\mathcal{N}}(0,\sigma^2)\) and \(g\) is absolutely continuous with \({\mathbb{E}}|g'(Z)|<\infty\): \[ {\mathbb{E}}[Zg(Z)]=\sigma^2{\mathbb{E}}[g'(Z)]. \] Multivariate: for \(X\sim{\mathcal{N}}(\mu,\Sigma)\), \({\mathbb{E}}[(X-\mu)g(X)]=\Sigma\,{\mathbb{E}}[\nabla g(X)]\).
ver: Gaussian smoothing gradients: \(\nabla_\mu{\mathbb{E}}_{{\mathcal{N}}(\mu,\sigma^2I)}f(X)=\tfrac{1}{\sigma^2}{\mathbb{E}}[(X-\mu)f(X)]\) — the evolution-strategies / zeroth-order gradient estimator.
Second order (Price's theorem): \(\nabla^2_\mu{\mathbb{E}} f={\mathbb{E}}\nabla^2f\).
cards.det: Proof: integration by parts using \(\phi'(z)=-z\phi(z)/\sigma^2\). It is the Gaussian special case of the log-derivative trick Log-derivative (score-function) trick & differentiating under the integral.
