cards.ex: Evolution strategies for policy search: \(\nabla_\theta{\mathbb{E}}_{{\varepsilon}}[J(\theta+\sigma{\varepsilon})]=\tfrac1\sigma{\mathbb{E}}[{\varepsilon} J(\theta+\sigma{\varepsilon})]\).
cards.use: Zeroth-order policy optimisation (ES, random search for LQR), Gaussian comparison proofs, SURE.

cards.name: Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality (Wasserstein-1)
cards.lay: The Wasserstein-1 distance (cheapest cost of moving one distribution's mass onto another) equals the largest difference in expectations over all 1-Lipschitz functions. Lipschitz value functions therefore change by at most \(L\cdot W_1\) when the next-state distribution moves.
cards.st: For probability measures \(P,Q\) with finite first moments on a metric space: \[ W_1(P,Q)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}{\mathbb{E}}_{(X,Y)\sim\pi}d(X,Y)=\sup_{{\lVert f\rVert}_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le1}\bigl({\mathbb{E}}_Pf-{\mathbb{E}}_Qf\bigr). \]
ver: Lipschitz MDPs: if \(W_1(P(\cdot|s,a),P(\cdot|s',a'))\le L_P d((s,a),(s',a'))\) and rewards are \(L_r\)-Lipschitz, \(Q^\star\) is \(\tfrac{L_r}{1-\gamma L_P}\)-Lipschitz when \(\gamma L_P<1\).
On \({\mathbb{R}}\): \(W_1(P,Q)=\int|F_P-F_Q|\) (CDF difference) Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality. TV is \(W_1\) under the discrete metric.
Bisimulation metrics are fixed points of a \(W_1\)-based operator.
cards.det: Simulation-lemma analogue in continuous spaces: \(|(P-\widehat P)V|\le{\lVert V\rVert}_{\mathrm{Lip}}W_1(P,\widehat P)\), replacing Hölder/TV when \(V\) is Lipschitz but the distributions are mutually singular (e.g. deterministic dynamics).
cards.ex: Deterministic dynamics \(s'=f(s,a)\) vs. learned \(\hat f\): \(W_1(\delta_{f(s,a)},\delta_{\hat f(s,a)})={\lVert f-\hat f\rVert}\), finite even though TV \(=1\).
cards.use: Model-based RL in continuous spaces, Lipschitz MDP theory, bisimulation metrics, distributional RL (Wasserstein contraction of the distributional Bellman operator).

cards.name: Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma
cards.lay: Any \(n\) points in high dimension can be mapped to \(O(\log n/{\varepsilon}^2)\) dimensions by a random linear map while preserving all pairwise distances up to \(1\pm{\varepsilon}\). Justifies random projections of features.
cards.st: For \(0<{\varepsilon}<1\) and \(n\) points in \({\mathbb{R}}^D\), if \(m\ge C{\varepsilon}^{-2}\log n\), a random Gaussian matrix \(G\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m\times D}\) scaled by \(1/\sqrt m\) satisfies, with high probability, for all pairs: \[ (1-{\varepsilon}){\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert}^2\le{\lVert Gx_i/\sqrt m-Gx_j/\sqrt m\rVert}^2\le(1+{\varepsilon}){\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert}^2. \]
ver: Sparse / fast JL transforms; subspace embeddings preserving all vectors of a \(d\)-dimensional subspace with \(m=O(d/{\varepsilon}^2)\).
cards.det: For a fixed vector, \({\lVert Gx\rVert}^2/{\lVert x\rVert}^2\) is a scaled \(\chi^2_m\) variable concentrating at rate \(e^{-cm{\varepsilon}^2}\) Sub-exponential variables & Bernstein condition; union bound over \(\binom n2\) pairs Union bound (Boole's inequality).
cards.ex: Compressing \(D=10^6\) sparse state features to \(m\approx10^3\) dimensions for linear value approximation while keeping inner products within \(\pm0.1\).
cards.use: Random-projection features in linear RL, sketching for large-scale LSTD, dimension reduction arguments.

cards.name: Brouwer & Kakutani fixed-point theorems
cards.lay: A continuous map from a compact convex set to itself always has a fixed point (Brouwer); set-valued versions (Kakutani) give existence of Nash equilibria. Unlike Banach, no contraction is needed — but there is no algorithm or rate either.
cards.st: (Brouwer) Every continuous \(f:K\to K\) on a nonempty compact convex \(K\subset{\mathbb{R}}^d\) has a fixed point. (Kakutani) Every upper hemicontinuous correspondence \(F:K\rightrightarrows K\) with nonempty convex closed values has \(x\in F(x)\).
ver: Nash's theorem: every finite game has a mixed-strategy equilibrium (via Kakutani on best responses).
Stationary Markov perfect equilibria exist in discounted stochastic games with finite states/actions (Fink 1964).
Schauder: infinite-dimensional (compact convex subsets of Banach spaces).
cards.det: Existence only: computing Brouwer/Nash fixed points is PPAD-hard in general, in contrast to the efficiently computable Banach fixed points Banach fixed-point theorem (contraction mapping).
cards.ex: General-sum Markov games: existence of stationary Nash equilibria is a Kakutani argument, even though learning them is computationally hard.
cards.use: Existence of equilibria in multi-agent RL, mean-field games, existence of solutions to non-contractive equations.

cards.name: Doeblin / minorisation condition & uniform ergodicity
cards.lay: If, from every state, the chain lands in a common distribution with probability at least \(\alpha\) after \(m\) steps, then it forgets its start geometrically fast: the distance to stationarity shrinks by \((1-\alpha)\) every \(m\) steps. Works on general (continuous) state spaces.
cards.st: If \(P^m(x,\cdot)\ge\alpha\,\nu(\cdot)\) for all \(x\) (some probability \(\nu\), \(\alpha>0\)), then \(P\) has a unique stationary \(\mu\) and for all \(x\), \(t\): \[ {\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(P^t(x,\cdot),\mu\bigr)\le(1-\alpha)^{\lfloor t/m\rfloor}. \]
ver: Dobrushin coefficient form: \(\delta(P^m)\le1-\alpha\) Mixing time & geometric ergodicity.
Drift + local minorisation (Harris' theorem; Meyn–Tweedie) for geometric ergodicity on non-compact spaces.
cards.det: Coupling proof Coupling inequality: every \(m\) steps, both copies can jump to a common draw from \(\nu\) with probability \(\alpha\); once coupled they stay together.
cards.ex: Any MDP with a “reset” action taken with probability \(\ge\alpha\) (or discounted MDPs viewed as chains restarting with probability \(1-\gamma\)) satisfies Doeblin with \(m=1\).
cards.use: Ergodicity assumptions in average-reward and continuous-state RL, mixing-time bounds, convergence of policy evaluation from trajectories.

cards.name: Davis–Kahan \(\sin\Theta\) theorem
cards.lay: Eigenvectors are stable under perturbation as long as the corresponding eigenvalue is well separated from the rest: the rotation angle is at most (perturbation size)/(eigengap).
cards.st: Let \(A\) and \(\widehat A=A+E\) be symmetric, \(u\) and \(\hat u\) unit eigenvectors for the \(i\)-th eigenvalue, and \(\delta=\min_{j\ne i}|\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_j(A)|\). Then \[ \sin\angle(u,\hat u)\le\frac{2{\lVert E\rVert}_2}{\delta}. \]
ver: Subspace version: \({\lVert \sin\Theta(U,\widehat U)\rVert}_F\le\tfrac{2\sqrt k{\lVert E\rVert}_2}{\delta}\) (Yu, Wang & Samworth 2015 variant).
Wedin's theorem for singular subspaces of non-symmetric matrices.
cards.det: Combine with matrix concentration Matrix Bernstein / matrix Chernoff (Tropp) to show empirical eigenvectors (features, spectral embeddings) converge at rate \({\lVert E\rVert}/\delta\).
cards.ex: Spectral learning of latent-state models (HMMs, POMDPs, latent MDPs): recovering the latent subspace from empirical moment matrices — an alternative to EM with global guarantees.
cards.use: Spectral methods for latent-variable RL, representation learning (proto-value functions, Laplacian features), PCA-based feature analyses.
